sentences.zh: 【宋紀十三】　柔兆敦牂，一年。

translations.literal: [Song Records 13] Rouzhao Dunzang; one year in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Song Records 13] Rouzhao Dunzang—one year in all.

sentences.zh: 太宗明皇帝上之下泰始二年（

translations.literal: The lower portion of the upper fascicle on Emperor Ming the Brilliant: Taishi year 2 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming the Brilliant, upper fascicle, lower portion—Taishi year 2 (

sentences.zh: 丙午，公元四六六年）

translations.literal: bingwu, 466 CE)
translations.idiomatic: bingwu, 466 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己丑朔，魏大赦，改元天安。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the jichou new moon, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Tian'an.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the jichou new moon, Northern Wei proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Tian'an.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，征會稽太守尋陽王子房為撫軍將軍，以巴陵王休若代之。

translations.literal: On guisi, the Prince of Xunyang Zifang, prefect of Kuaiji, was summoned to serve as General Who Pacifies the Army; the Prince of Baling Xiuruo was appointed to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, the court summoned Kuaiji prefect Prince of Xunyang Liu Zifang to serve as General Who Pacifies the Army and appointed Prince of Baling Liu Xiuruo in his place.

sentences.zh: 甲午，中外戒嚴。

translations.literal: On jiawu, martial law was declared throughout the court and the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Emperor Ming declared martial law throughout the court and the realm.

sentences.zh: 以司徒建安王休仁都督征討諸軍事，車騎將軍、江州刺史王玄謨副之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jian'an Xiuren, Minister of Works, was made commander-in-chief of all armies for the punitive campaign, with General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Jiangzhou Wang Xuemo as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren, Minister of Works, was placed in overall command of the punitive armies, with General of Chariots and Cavalry and Jiangzhou inspector Wang Xuemo as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 休仁軍於南州，以沈攸之為尋陽太守，將兵屯虎檻。

translations.literal: Xiuren encamped his army in the southern provinces; Shen Youzhi was appointed prefect of Xunyang and led troops to garrison Hujian.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren encamped his army in the southern provinces, appointed Shen Youzhi prefect of Xunyang, and sent him to garrison Hujian with his troops.

sentences.zh: 時玄謨未發，前鋒凡十軍，絡繹繼至。

translations.literal: At this time Xuemo had not yet set out, but the vanguard—ten armies in all—arrived in an unbroken stream.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuemo had not yet marched out, but the vanguard alone comprised ten armies, arriving one after another without pause.

sentences.zh: 每夜各立姓號，不相稟受。

translations.literal: Each night they established their own rallying calls and did not take orders from one another.
translations.idiomatic: Each night every unit set up its own watchword, and none obeyed the others' commands.

sentences.zh: 攸之謂諸將曰：「今眾軍姓號不同，若有耕夫、漁父夜相呵叱，便致駭亂，取敗之道也。

translations.literal: Youzhi said to the generals: "Now the various armies use different rallying calls. If a farmer or fisherman should shout at one another in the night, panic and disorder would follow—that is the road to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi told the generals: "Our armies all use different watchwords tonight. If a farmer or fisherman should shout back and forth in the dark, we would throw ourselves into panic—that is how battles are lost.

sentences.zh: 請就一軍取號。」

translations.literal: I ask that we all adopt a single army's call."
translations.idiomatic: Let us all adopt one army's watchword."

sentences.zh: 眾鹹從之。

translations.literal: All assented.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone agreed.

sentences.zh: 鄧琬稱說符瑞，詐稱受路太后璽書，帥將佐上尊於晉安王子勳。

translations.literal: Deng Wan cited omens and portents and falsely claimed to have received a sealed edict from Empress Dowager Lu; he led his officers in offering supreme honor to the Prince of Jin'an Zixun.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan proclaimed auspicious signs, forged a claim that he had received the imperial seal-edict of Empress Dowager Lu, and led his officers in elevating Prince of Jin'an Liu Zixun to the throne.

sentences.zh: 乙未，子勳即皇帝位於尋陽，改元義嘉。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Zixun assumed the imperial throne at Xunyang and changed the era name to Yijia.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Zixun took the imperial throne at Xunyang and proclaimed the era name Yijia.

sentences.zh: 以安陸王子綏為司徒、揚州刺史；

translations.literal: The Prince of Anlu Zisui was appointed Minister of Works and Inspector of Yangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Anlu Liu Zisui was made Minister of Works and Yangzhou inspector;

sentences.zh: 尋陽王子房、臨海王子頊並加開府儀同三司；

translations.literal: the Princes of Xunyang Zifang and Linhai Zixiang were both granted the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies;
translations.idiomatic: Princes of Xunyang Liu Zifang and Linhai Liu Zixiang were both granted the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies;

sentences.zh: 以鄧琬為尚書右僕射，張悅為吏部尚書，袁顗加尚書左僕射；

translations.literal: Deng Wan was made Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Zhang Yue Minister of Personnel, and Yuan Yi was additionally appointed Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan was appointed Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Zhang Yue Minister of Personnel, and Yuan Yi was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 自餘將佐及諸州郡，除官進爵號各有差。

translations.literal: among the remaining officers and the various provinces and commanderies, appointments, promotions, and noble titles were distributed with distinctions.
translations.idiomatic: the remaining commanders, officials, and provincial and commandery posts received appointments, promotions, and noble titles according to rank.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以征虜司馬申令孫為徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Shen Lingsun, Chief of Staff for the Campaign against Barbarians, was appointed Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Shen Lingsun, chief of staff for the campaign against barbarians, was appointed Xuzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 令孫，坦之子也。

translations.literal: Lingsun was the son of Shen Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Lingsun was the son of Shen Tan.

sentences.zh: 置司州於義陽，以義陽內史龐孟虯為司州刺史。

translations.literal: The province of Sizhou was established at Yiyang, and Pang Mengjiao, Administrator of Yiyang, was appointed Inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhou was established at Yiyang, and Yiyang administrator Pang Mengjiao was made its inspector.

sentences.zh: 徐州刺史薛安都、冀州刺史清河崔道固皆舉兵應尋陽。

translations.literal: Xue Andu, Inspector of Xuzhou, and Cui Daogu of Qinghe, Inspector of Jizhou, both raised armies in support of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou inspector Xue Andu and Jizhou inspector Cui Daogu of Qinghe both took up arms for the Xunyang regime.

sentences.zh: 上徵兵於青州刺史沈文秀，文秀遣其將平原劉彌之等將兵赴建康。

translations.literal: The emperor called for troops from Shen Wenxiu, Inspector of Qingzhou; Wenxiu sent his generals Liu Mizhi of Pingyuan and others to lead troops to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned troops from Qingzhou inspector Shen Wenxiu, who sent his generals Liu Mizhi of Pingyuan and others to march on Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 會薛安都遣使邀文秀，文秀更令彌之等應安都。

translations.literal: When Xue Andu sent envoys to invite Wenxiu, Wenxiu ordered Mizhi and the others to join Andu instead.
translations.idiomatic: But Xue Andu sent envoys to win Shen Wenxiu over, and Wenxiu then ordered Mizhi and his men to join Andu.

sentences.zh: 濟陰太守申闡據睢陵應建康，安都遣其從子直閣將軍索兒、太原太守清河傅靈越等攻之。

translations.literal: Shen Chan, Prefect of Jiyin, held Suiling for Jiankang; Andu sent his nephew Suo Er, General of the Direct Attendants, and Fu Lingyue of Qinghe, Prefect of Taiyuan, and others to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyin prefect Shen Chan held Suiling for Jiankang; Andu sent his nephew Suo Er, a general of the direct attendants, together with Taiyuan prefect Fu Lingyue of Qinghe and others to attack him.

sentences.zh: 闡，令孫之弟也。

translations.literal: Chan was the younger brother of Lingsun.
translations.idiomatic: Chan was Shen Lingsun's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 安都婿裴祖隆守下邳，劉彌之至下邳，更以所領應建康，襲擊祖隆。

translations.literal: Pei Zulong, Andu's son-in-law, held Xiapi; when Liu Mizhi reached Xiapi, he turned his command to Jiankang's side and attacked Zulong.
translations.idiomatic: Andu's son-in-law Pei Zulong held Xiapi; when Liu Mizhi arrived there, he switched his forces back to Jiankang and struck at Zulong.

sentences.zh: 祖隆兵敗，與征北參軍垣崇祖奔彭城。

translations.literal: Zulong was defeated and fled with Yuan Chongzu, Staff Officer for the Northern Campaign, to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zulong was beaten and fled with northern campaign staff officer Yuan Chongzu to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 崇祖，護之之從子也。

translations.literal: Chongzu was a nephew of Yuan Huzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzu was a nephew of Yuan Huzhi.

sentences.zh: 彌之族人北海太守懷恭、從子善明皆舉兵以應彌之，薛索兒聞之，釋睢陵，引兵擊彌之。

translations.literal: Mizhi's clansman Huai Gong, Prefect of Beihai, and his nephew Shanming both raised troops in support of Mizhi; when Xue Suo Er heard of this, he abandoned Suiling and led his army against Mizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Mizhi's kinsman Beihai prefect Huai Gong and his nephew Shanming both took up arms for him; hearing this, Xue Suo Er abandoned the siege of Suiling and marched against Mizhi.

sentences.zh: 彌之戰敗，走保北海。

translations.literal: Mizhi was defeated and fled to hold Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Mizhi was defeated and withdrew to defend Beihai.

sentences.zh: 申令孫進據淮陽，請降於索兒。

translations.literal: Shen Lingsun advanced and seized Huaiyang, then offered surrender to Suo Er.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Lingsun seized Huaiyang and offered to surrender to Suo Er.

sentences.zh: 龐孟虯亦不受命，舉兵應尋陽。

translations.literal: Pang Mengjiao likewise refused his orders and raised troops in support of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Mengjiao also defied the court and took up arms for Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 帝召尋陽王長史行會稽郡事孔覬為太子詹事，以平西司馬庾業代之；

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Kong Kai, Chief Administrator of the Prince of Xunyang and acting Administrator of Kuaiji Commandery, to serve as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and replaced him with Yu Ye, Chief of Staff for the Western Pacification;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Kong Kai, chief administrator to the Prince of Xunyang who was also acting Kuaiji administrator, to serve as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and sent Yu Ye, chief of staff for the western pacification, to replace him;

sentences.zh: 又遣都水使者孔璪入東慰勞。

translations.literal: he also sent Kong Zuan, Commissioner for Waterworks, into the east to offer comfort and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: he also dispatched waterworks commissioner Kong Zuan eastward to offer comfort and rewards.

sentences.zh: 璪說凱以「建康虛弱，不如擁五郡以應袁、鄧。」

translations.literal: Zuan urged Kai: "Jiankang is weak; you would do better to rally the five commanderies and join Yuan and Deng."
translations.idiomatic: Zuan urged Kai: "Jiankang is feeble; you would do better to rally the five commanderies and side with Yuan Yi and Deng Wan."

sentences.zh: 覬遂發兵，馳檄奉尋陽。

translations.literal: Kai thereupon raised troops and sent out proclamations in support of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kai thereupon mobilized his forces and issued urgent proclamations declaring for Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 吳郡太守顧琛、吳興太守王曇生、義興太守劉延熙、晉陵太守袁標皆據郡應之。

translations.literal: Gu Chen, Prefect of Wu Commandery; Wang Tansheng, Prefect of Wuxing; Liu Yanxi, Prefect of Yixing; and Yuan Biao, Prefect of Jinling, all held their commanderies in response.
translations.idiomatic: Wu prefect Gu Chen, Wuxing prefect Wang Tansheng, Yixing prefect Liu Yanxi, and Jinling prefect Yuan Biao all seized their commanderies and joined him.

sentences.zh: 上又以庾業代延熙為義興，業至長塘湖，即與延熙合。

translations.literal: The emperor also sent Yu Ye to replace Yanxi as Prefect of Yixing, but when Ye reached Changtang Lake he joined forces with Yanxi at once.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also sent Yu Ye to replace Liu Yanxi as Yixing prefect, but when Ye reached Changtang Lake he immediately joined forces with Yanxi.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史蕭惠開，聞晉安王子勳舉兵，集將佐謂之曰：「湘東，太祖之昭；

translations.literal: Xiao Huikai, Inspector of Yizhou, on hearing that the Prince of Jin'an Zixun had raised troops, gathered his officers and said to them: "The Prince of Xiangdong is a son of the Founder by a primary consort;
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhou inspector Xiao Huikai heard that Prince of Jin'an Liu Zixun had taken up arms, he assembled his officers and said: "Prince of Xiangdong is a son of the dynastic founder by a primary consort;

sentences.zh: 晉安，世祖之穆；

translations.literal: the Prince of Jin'an is a son of Emperor Shizu by a secondary consort;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jin'an is a son of Emperor Shizu by a secondary consort;

sentences.zh: 其於當璧，並無不可。

translations.literal: as to who should receive the jade disc of rule, neither is ineligible.
translations.idiomatic: as to who should receive the throne, neither claim is inherently invalid.

sentences.zh: 但景和雖昏，本是世祖之嗣；

translations.literal: Yet although Emperor Jinghe was benighted, he was originally Shizu's heir;
translations.idiomatic: Yet although Emperor Jinghe was benighted, he was still Shizu's legitimate heir;

sentences.zh: 不任社稷，其次猶多。

translations.literal: unfit though he was to bear the altars of state, there were still many others who came next in line.
translations.idiomatic: unfit though he was to bear the altars of state, many others still stood ahead in the succession.

sentences.zh: 吾荷世祖之眷，當推奉九江。」

translations.literal: I have received Shizu's favor and ought to support and uphold Jiujiang."
translations.idiomatic: I owe Shizu a debt of favor and ought to support and uphold Jiujiang."

sentences.zh: 乃遣巴郡太守費欣壽將五千人東下。

translations.literal: He then sent Fei Xinshou, Prefect of Ba Commandery, eastward with five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Ba prefect Fei Xinshou eastward with five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 於是湘州行事何慧文、廣州刺史袁曇遠、梁州刺史柳元怙、山陽太守程天祚皆附於子勳。

translations.literal: Thereupon He Huiwen, acting Administrator of Xiangzhou; Yuan Tanyuan, Inspector of Guangzhou; Liu Yuanku, Inspector of Liangzhou; and Cheng Tianzuo, Prefect of Shanyang, all attached themselves to Zixun.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Xiangzhou acting administrator He Huiwen, Guangzhou inspector Yuan Tanyuan, Liangzhou inspector Liu Yuanku, and Shanyang prefect Cheng Tianzuo all declared for Zixun.

sentences.zh: 元怙，元景之從兄也。

translations.literal: Yuanku was a cousin of Liu Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanku was a cousin of Liu Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 是歲，四方貢計皆歸尋陽，朝廷所保，唯丹陽、淮南等數郡，其間諸縣或應子勳。

translations.literal: That year, tribute and tax reports from all quarters went to Xunyang; what the court still held were only a few commanderies such as Danyang and Huainan, and even among them some counties sided with Zixun.
translations.idiomatic: That year, tribute and tax reports from every quarter went to Xunyang; the court retained only a handful of commanderies such as Danyang and Huainan, and even within those some counties declared for Zixun.

sentences.zh: 東兵已至永世，宮省危懼。

translations.literal: Eastern troops had already reached Yongshi, and the palace was gripped by fear.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern rebel troops had already reached Yongshi, and the palace was gripped by fear.

sentences.zh: 上集群臣以謀成敗。

translations.literal: The emperor assembled the ministers to deliberate on success or failure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assembled his ministers to deliberate on how the war would turn.

sentences.zh: 蔡興宗曰：「今普天同叛，人有異志。

translations.literal: Cai Xingzong said: "Now the whole realm rebels together, and every man harbors his own intent.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xingzong said: "The whole realm has risen in rebellion, and every man harbors his own intent.

sentences.zh: 宜鎮之以靜，至信待人。

translations.literal: You should calm them with stillness and treat people with utmost trust.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should calm them with stillness and treat people with utmost trust.

sentences.zh: 叛者親戚布在宮省，若繩之以法，則士崩立至，宜明罪不相及之義。

translations.literal: The kinsmen of rebels are spread through the palace offices; if you bind them with the law, the army will collapse at once. You should make clear the principle that guilt does not extend to relatives.
translations.idiomatic: The kinsmen of rebels fill the palace offices; if you punish them by law, the army will collapse at once. Your Majesty should make clear that guilt does not extend to relatives.

sentences.zh: 物情既定，人有戰心，六軍精勇，器甲犀利，以待不習之兵，其勢相萬耳。

translations.literal: Once popular sentiment is settled, men will have the will to fight; the Six Armies are elite and brave, their weapons sharp—awaiting troops unaccustomed to war, their advantage is ten thousand to one.
translations.idiomatic: Once hearts are settled, men will fight willingly; the Six Armies are elite and brave, their arms keen—against troops unaccustomed to war, our advantage is ten thousand to one.

sentences.zh: 願陛下勿憂。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty not to worry."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty not to worry."

sentences.zh: 上善之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 建武司馬劉順說豫州刺史殷琰使應尋陽，琰以家在建康，未許。

translations.literal: Liu Shun, Chief of Staff for the Jianwu campaign, urged Yin Yan, Inspector of Yuzhou, to join Xunyang; Yan, whose family was in Jiankang, did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu chief of staff Liu Shun urged Yuzhou inspector Yin Yan to join Xunyang, but Yan, whose family was in Jiankang, refused.

sentences.zh: 右衛將軍柳光世自省內出奔彭城，過壽陽，言建康必不能守。

translations.literal: Liu Guangshi, General of the Right Guard, fled from within the palace to Pengcheng; passing Shouyang, he declared that Jiankang could certainly not be held.
translations.idiomatic: Right Guard general Liu Guangshi fled the capital for Pengcheng; passing Shouyang, he declared that Jiankang could not possibly be held.

sentences.zh: 琰信之，且素無部曲，為土豪前右軍參軍杜叔寶等所制，不得已而從之。

translations.literal: Yan believed him; moreover, he had never had troops of his own and was controlled by local strongmen such as Du Shubao, former Staff Officer of the Right Army, and had no choice but to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yan believed him; moreover, he had never commanded troops of his own and was controlled by local strongmen such as former Right Army staff officer Du Shubao, so he had no choice but to follow.

sentences.zh: 琰以叔寶為長史，內外軍事，皆叔寶專之。

translations.literal: Yan appointed Shubao Chief Administrator; all military affairs within and without were monopolized by Shubao.
translations.idiomatic: Yan made Shubao his chief administrator, and Shubao monopolized all military affairs.

sentences.zh: 上謂蔡興宗曰：「諸處未平，殷琰已復同逆；

translations.literal: The emperor said to Cai Xingzong: "The various regions are not yet pacified, and Yin Yan has again joined the rebels;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Cai Xingzong: "The regions are not yet pacified, and Yin Yan has joined the rebels again;

sentences.zh: 頃日人情雲何？

translations.literal: what is popular sentiment these days?
translations.idiomatic: what is the mood among the people these days?

sentences.zh: 事當濟不？」

translations.literal: Will the affair succeed or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Will we prevail?"

sentences.zh: 興宗曰：「逆之與順，臣無以辨。

translations.literal: Xingzong said: "As to who is rebel and who is loyal, your servant cannot distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong said: "As to who is rebel and who is loyal, I cannot tell.

sentences.zh: 今商旅斷絕，米甚豐賤，四方雲合，而人情更安。

translations.literal: Now merchants and travelers are cut off, yet grain is very plentiful and cheap; from all quarters men gather like clouds, yet popular sentiment grows calmer.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants and travelers are cut off, yet grain is plentiful and cheap; rebels gather from every quarter, yet the people's hearts grow calmer.

sentences.zh: 以此卜之，清蕩可必。

translations.literal: Judging by this, complete pacification is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by this, complete victory is certain.

sentences.zh: 但臣之所憂，更在事後，猶羊公言：『既平之後，方當勞聖慮耳。』」

translations.literal: Yet what your servant fears lies rather afterward, as Duke Yang said: 'Only after they are pacified will Your Sagely Concern truly be taxed.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet what I fear lies afterward, as Duke Yang said: 'Only after they are pacified will Your Majesty's cares truly begin.'

sentences.zh: 上曰：「誠如卿言。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "It is indeed as you say."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You speak truly."

sentences.zh: 上知琰附尋陽非本意，乃更厚撫其家以招之。

translations.literal: Knowing that Yan's adherence to Xunyang was not his true intent, the emperor treated his family with still greater kindness to win him over.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Yan's adherence to Xunyang was not his true intent, the emperor treated his family with still greater kindness to win him back.

sentences.zh: 汝南、新蔡二郡太守周矜起兵於懸瓠以應建康。

translations.literal: Zhou Jin, joint Prefect of Runan and Xincai commanderies, raised troops at Xuanyi in support of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jin, prefect of Runan and Xincai, raised troops at Xuanyi for Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 袁顗誘矜司馬汝南常珍奇執矜，斬之，以珍奇代為太守。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi induced Zhou Jin's Chief of Staff, Chang Zhenqi of Runan, to seize Jin and behead him, then installed Zhenqi as prefect in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi induced Jin's chief of staff Chang Zhenqi of Runan to seize and behead him, then installed Zhenqi as prefect in his place.

sentences.zh: 上使冗從僕射垣榮祖還徐州說薛安都，安都曰：「今京都無百里地，不論攻圍取勝，自可拍手笑殺；

translations.literal: The emperor sent Yuan Rongzu, Vice Director of Attendant Retainers, back to Xuzhou to persuade Xue Andu; Andu said: "Now the capital has not a hundred li of territory left; never mind attacking or besieging to win—one may simply clap one's hands and laugh them to death;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent attendant retainer vice director Yuan Rongzu back to Xuzhou to persuade Xue Andu; Andu said: "The capital has scarcely a hundred li of territory left; never mind attacking or besieging to win—you can simply clap your hands and laugh them to death;

sentences.zh: 且我不欲負孝武。」

translations.literal: moreover, I do not wish to betray Emperor Xiaowu."
translations.idiomatic: moreover, I do not wish to betray Emperor Xiaowu."

sentences.zh: 榮祖曰：「孝武之行，足致餘殃，今雖天下雷同，正是速死，無能為也。」

translations.literal: Rongzu said: "Emperor Xiaowu's conduct was enough to bring lingering calamity; though the whole realm now echoes in rebellion, that is precisely the road to swift ruin—they can accomplish nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Rongzu said: "Emperor Xiaowu's conduct brought lingering calamity in its train; though the whole realm now rises together, that is precisely the road to swift ruin—they can accomplish nothing."

sentences.zh: 安都不從，因留榮祖使為將。

translations.literal: Andu would not listen and detained Rongzu to serve as a general.
translations.idiomatic: Andu would not listen and detained Rongzu to serve as one of his generals.

sentences.zh: 榮祖，崇祖之從父兄也。

translations.literal: Rongzu was a cousin of Chongzu on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Rongzu was Yuan Chongzu's paternal cousin.

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史殷孝祖之甥司法參軍穎川葛僧韶，請殷孝祖入朝，上遣之。

translations.literal: Ge Sengshao of Yingchuan, Judicial Staff Officer and nephew of Yin Xiaozu, Inspector of Yanzhou, asked that Xiaozu come to court; the emperor sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Sengshao of Yingchuan, judicial staff officer and nephew of Yanzhou inspector Yin Xiaozu, asked that Xiaozu come to court; the emperor sent for him.

sentences.zh: 時薛索兒屯據津逕，僧韶間行得至，說孝祖曰：「景和凶狂，開闢未有；

translations.literal: At this time Xue Suo Er held the crossing at Jinjin; Sengshao made his way through by hidden routes and reached Xiaozu, saying to him: "Emperor Jinghe was fierce and mad beyond anything since the founding;
translations.idiomatic: Xue Suo Er then held the crossing at Jinjin; Sengshao made his way through by hidden routes and told Xiaozu: "Emperor Jinghe was fierce and mad beyond anything since the founding;

sentences.zh: 朝野危極，假命漏刻。

translations.literal: court and realm were at the utmost peril, their lives prolonged only by the drip of the water clock.
translations.idiomatic: court and realm stood at the brink of ruin, their lives prolonged only hour by hour.

sentences.zh: 主上夷山翦暴，更造天地，國亂朝危，宜立長君。

translations.literal: Our lord leveled mountains and cut down the violent, remaking heaven and earth; with the state in turmoil and the court in peril, a mature ruler ought to be established.
translations.idiomatic: Our lord leveled mountains and cut down the violent, remaking heaven and earth; with the state in turmoil and the court in peril, a mature ruler ought to be enthroned.

sentences.zh: 而群迷相煽，構造無端，貪利幼弱，競懷希望。

translations.literal: Yet the deluded masses incite one another, fabricating causes without reason, greedy for profit from a young and weak ruler, each clutching his own hope.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the deluded masses incite one another, fabricating grievances without cause, greedy for profit from a young and weak ruler, each nursing his own hope.

sentences.zh: 使天道助逆，群凶事申，則主幼時艱，權柄不一，兵難互起，豈有自容之地！

translations.literal: If heaven should aid the rebels and the wicked succeed, then with a young lord and hard times, power would not be unified, military troubles would arise one after another—where would there be room for you to preserve yourself!
translations.idiomatic: If heaven aids the rebels and the wicked prevail, then with a young sovereign and hard times, power will not be unified and wars will break out everywhere—where will you find room to preserve yourself!

sentences.zh: 舅少有立功之志，若能控濟主勇，還奉朝廷，非唯匡主靜亂，乃可以垂名竹帛。」

translations.literal: Uncle, you have long cherished the will to achieve merit; if you can marshal the brave men of Jizhou and return to serve the court, you will not only restore the ruler and pacify disorder—you may leave your name on silk and bamboo."
translations.idiomatic: Uncle, you have long wished to win merit; if you rally the brave men of Jizhou and return to serve the court, you will not only restore the ruler and pacify disorder—you may leave your name in history."

sentences.zh: 孝祖具問朝廷消息，僧韶隨方酬譬，並陳兵甲精強，主上欲委以前驅之任。

translations.literal: Xiaozu questioned him fully about news from court; Sengshao answered as occasion required and also described the strength of arms and armor, saying that the sovereign wished to entrust him with the vanguard command.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozu questioned him fully about news from court; Sengshao answered to each point and described the army's strength, saying the sovereign wished to entrust him with the vanguard command.

sentences.zh: 孝祖即日委妻子於瑕丘，帥文武二千人，隨僧韶還建康。

translations.literal: That same day Xiaozu left his wife and children at Xiaqiu and led two thousand civil and military men back to Jiankang with Sengshao.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Xiaozu left his wife and children at Xiaqiu and led two thousand civil and military followers back to Jiankang with Sengshao.

sentences.zh: 時四方皆附尋陽，朝廷唯保丹陽一郡；

translations.literal: At this time all quarters had attached themselves to Xunyang, and the court held only the single commandery of Danyang;
translations.idiomatic: At this time every quarter had declared for Xunyang, and the court held only Danyang commandery;

sentences.zh: 而永世令孔景宣復叛，義興兵垂至延陵，內外憂危，鹹欲奔散。

translations.literal: yet the magistrate of Yongshi, Kong Jingxuan, rebelled again, Yixing troops were about to reach Yanling, and within and without all were anxious and imperiled, each wishing to flee and scatter.
translations.idiomatic: yet Yongshi magistrate Kong Jingxuan rebelled again, Yixing troops were about to reach Yanling, and within and without all were anxious and imperiled, each wishing to flee.

sentences.zh: 孝祖忽至，眾力不少，並傖楚壯士，人情大安。

translations.literal: When Xiaozu arrived suddenly, his force was not small, and all were stalwart men of Chu; popular sentiment grew greatly reassured.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozu arrived suddenly, his force was substantial, and all were stalwart men of Chu; hearts throughout the capital were greatly reassured.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，進孝祖號撫軍將軍，假節、督前鋒諸軍事，遣向虎檻，寵賚甚厚。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Xiaozu was advanced to General Who Pacifies the Army, given provisional credentials and command of all vanguard forces, and sent toward Hujian with very generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Xiaozu was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army, given provisional credentials and overall command of the vanguard, and sent toward Hujian with very generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 初，上遣東平畢眾敬詣兗州募人，至彭城，薛安都以利害說之，矯上命以眾敬行兗州事，眾敬從之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor had sent Bi Zhongjing of Dongping to Yanzhou to recruit men; when he reached Pengcheng, Xue Andu persuaded him with arguments of advantage and harm and forged an imperial order appointing Zhongjing acting Administrator of Yanzhou; Zhongjing complied.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the emperor had sent Bi Zhongjing of Dongping to Yanzhou to recruit men; when he reached Pengcheng, Xue Andu persuaded him with arguments of gain and loss and forged an imperial order making him acting Yanzhou administrator; Zhongjing complied.

sentences.zh: 殷孝祖使司馬劉文石守瑕丘，眾敬引兵擊殺之。

translations.literal: Yin Xiaozu had Liu Wenshi, his Chief of Staff, hold Xiaqiu; Zhongjing led troops, attacked, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Xiaozu had his chief of staff Liu Wenshi hold Xiaqiu; Zhongjing led troops against him and killed him.

sentences.zh: 安都素與孝祖有隙，使眾敬殺孝祖諸子。

translations.literal: Andu had long been at odds with Xiaozu and had Zhongjing kill all of Xiaozu's sons.
translations.idiomatic: Andu had long been at odds with Xiaozu and had Zhongjing kill all of Xiaozu's sons.

sentences.zh: 州境皆附之，唯東平太守申纂據無鹽，不從。

translations.literal: The whole province attached itself to him; only Shen Zuan, Prefect of Dongping, held Wuyan and would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The whole province submitted to him; only Dongping prefect Shen Zuan held Wuyan and refused.

sentences.zh: 纂，鐘之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Zuan was a great-grandson of Shen Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan was a great-grandson of Shen Zhong.

sentences.zh: 丙午，上親總兵，出頓中堂。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the emperor personally took command of the army and encamped at Zhongtang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, the emperor personally took command of the army and encamped at Zhongtang.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以山陽王休祐為豫州刺史，督輔國將軍彭城劉勉、寧朔將軍廣陵呂安國等諸軍西討殷琰。

translations.literal: On xinhai, the Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was appointed Inspector of Yuzhou and placed in command of the armies of Supporting-the-State General Liu Mian of Pengcheng, Pacifying-the-North General Lu Anguo of Guangling, and others for a western campaign against Yin Yan.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Prince of Shanyang Liu Xiuyou was appointed Yuzhou inspector and placed in command of Supporting-the-State general Liu Mian of Pengcheng, Pacifying-the-North general Lu Anguo of Guangling, and others for a western campaign against Yin Yan.

sentences.zh: 巴陵王休若督建威將軍吳興沈懷明、尚書張永、輔國將軍蕭道成等諸軍東討孔凱。

translations.literal: The Prince of Baling Xiuruo was placed in command of the armies of Establishing Might General Shen Huaiming of Wuxing, Minister of Works Zhang Yong, Supporting-the-State General Xiao Daocheng, and others for an eastern campaign against Kong Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Baling Liu Xiuruo was placed in command of Establishing Might general Shen Huaiming of Wuxing, Minister Zhang Yong, Supporting-the-State general Xiao Daocheng, and others for an eastern campaign against Kong Kai.

sentences.zh: 時將士多東方人，父兄子弟皆已附凱。

translations.literal: At the time most officers and soldiers were men from the east; their fathers, elder brothers, and younger brothers had all already attached themselves to Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the officers and soldiers were easterners; fathers, elder brothers, and sons in their families had already gone over to Kong Kai.

sentences.zh: 上因送軍，普加宣示曰：「朕方務德簡刑，使父子兄弟罪不相及，助順同逆者，一以所從為斷。

translations.literal: As the emperor therefore escorted the army forth, he broadly proclaimed and declared: "We are now devoted to virtue and simplifying punishments, so that crimes of fathers and sons and brothers do not extend to one another; for those who aid the obedient or share in rebellion, judgment shall be wholly according to whom they followed.
translations.idiomatic: As he sent the army forth, the emperor issued a general proclamation: "I am devoted to virtue and lenient punishment; crimes shall not extend from father to son or from brother to brother. Those who aided the loyal or followed the rebels will be judged solely by the side they joined.

sentences.zh: 卿等當深達此懷，勿以親戚為慮也。」

translations.literal: You all should deeply understand this intent; do not take kinfolk as a source of worry."
translations.idiomatic: You must take this intent deeply to heart and do not fret over your relatives."

sentences.zh: 眾於是大悅。

translations.literal: The masses thereupon were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were greatly heartened.

sentences.zh: 凡叛者親黨在建康者，皆使居職如故。

translations.literal: All kin and associates of rebels who were in Jiankang were made to hold their posts as before.
translations.idiomatic: All relatives and associates of rebels who were in Jiankang were allowed to remain in their posts unchanged.

sentences.zh: 壬子，路太后殂。

translations.literal: On renzi, Empress Dowager Lu died.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Empress Dowager Lu died.

sentences.zh: 孔覬遣其孫曇瓘等軍於晉陵九里，部陳甚盛。

translations.literal: Kong Xuan sent his grandson Tan Guan and others with an army at Jiuli in Jinling; their battle array was very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xuan sent his grandson Tan Guan and others to encamp at Jiuli in Jinling; their battle array was formidable.

sentences.zh: 沈懷明至奔牛，所令寡弱，乃築壘自固。

translations.literal: Shen Huaiming reached Benniu; the troops under his command were few and weak, so he built fortifications to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huaiming reached Benniu; his command was few and weak, so he built fortifications to hold his position.

sentences.zh: 張永至曲阿，未知懷明安否；

translations.literal: Zhang Yong reached Qu'e but did not know whether Huaiming was safe;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong reached Qu'e but did not know whether Shen Huaiming was safe;

sentences.zh: 百姓驚擾，永退還延陵，就巴陵王休若，諸將帥鹹勸休若退保破岡。

translations.literal: The common people were alarmed and disturbed; Yong withdrew to Yanling and joined the Prince of Baling Xiuruo; all the generals urged Xiuruo to withdraw and hold Pogang.
translations.idiomatic: The populace panicked; Zhang Yong withdrew to Yanling and joined Prince of Baling Liu Xiuruo; all the commanders urged Xiuruo to fall back and hold Pogang.

sentences.zh: 其日，大寒，風雪甚猛，塘埭決壞，眾無固心。

translations.literal: That day was bitterly cold; wind and snow were very fierce; embankments burst and were ruined; the masses had no firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: That day brought bitter cold and fierce wind and snow; dikes burst, and the troops lost heart.

sentences.zh: 休若宣令：「敢有言退者斬！」

translations.literal: Xiuruo proclaimed the order: "Whoever dares speak of retreat shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiuruo proclaimed the order: "Whoever dares speak of retreat shall be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 眾小定，乃築壘息甲。

translations.literal: The masses were somewhat settled; they then built fortifications and rested the armor.
translations.idiomatic: The men steadied somewhat; they then built fortifications and rested their arms.

sentences.zh: 尋得懷明書，賊定未進，軍主劉亮又至，兵力轉盛，人情乃安。

translations.literal: Before long they received Huaiming's letter: the rebels were settled and had not advanced; army commander Liu Liang also arrived; military strength grew; morale then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they received word from Huaiming that the rebels were holding still and had not advanced; army commander Liu Liang also arrived, strength increased, and morale settled.

sentences.zh: 亮，懷慎之從孫也。

translations.literal: Liang was a collateral descendant of Huaishen.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was a collateral descendant of Shen Huaishen.

sentences.zh: 殿中御史吳喜以主書事世祖，稍遷至河東太守。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Censor Wu Xi had served as master of documents under Emperor Xiaowu and was gradually promoted to Administrator of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant censor Wu Xi had served as master of documents under Emperor Xiaowu and was gradually promoted to Hedong administrator.

sentences.zh: 至是，請得精兵三百，致死於東。

translations.literal: At this time he requested and obtained three hundred picked troops to give his life in the east.
translations.idiomatic: At this juncture he asked for three hundred elite troops and vowed to stake his life in the east.

sentences.zh: 上假喜建武將軍，簡羽林勇士配之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted Xi the acting title Establishing Might General and selected elite guardsmen of the Feathered Forest to assign to him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave Xi the acting rank of Establishing Might general and picked elite Feathered Forest guards to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 議者以「喜刀筆主者，未嘗為將，不可遣。」

translations.literal: Those who deliberated held that "Xi is a brush-and-knife chief clerk who has never served as a general; he cannot be sent."
translations.idiomatic: Counselors argued that "Xi is a clerical chief who has never commanded troops and must not be sent."

sentences.zh: 中書舍人巢尚之曰：「喜昔隨沈慶之，屢經軍旅，性既勇決，又習戰陳；

translations.literal: Central Palace Gentleman Chao Shangzhi said: "Xi formerly followed Shen Qingzhi and repeatedly went through campaigns; by nature he is brave and decisive, and he is also practiced in battle arrays;
translations.idiomatic: Central palace gentleman Chao Shangzhi said: "Xi once followed Shen Qingzhi through many campaigns; he is brave and resolute by nature and skilled in battle formations;

sentences.zh: 若能任之，必有成績。

translations.literal: if he can be entrusted with command, he is sure to achieve results.
translations.idiomatic: if you entrust him, he is sure to achieve results.

sentences.zh: 諸人紛紜，皆是不別才耳。」

translations.literal: The many voices clamoring are all simply failure to distinguish talent."
translations.idiomatic: All this clamor is simply failure to recognize talent."

sentences.zh: 乃遣之。

translations.literal: He was then dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: He was then sent out.

sentences.zh: 喜先時數奉使東吳，性寬厚，所至人並懷之。

translations.literal: Xi had several times previously been sent on missions to Eastern Wu; his nature was generous and kind; wherever he went people all cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had been sent on missions to the Wu region several times before; his nature was generous, and wherever he went the people cherished him.

sentences.zh: 百姓聞吳河東來，皆望風降散，故喜所至克捷。

translations.literal: When the common people heard that Wu of Hedong was coming, they all scattered in surrender before the wind; therefore wherever Xi went he achieved swift success.
translations.idiomatic: When the people heard that Wu of Hedong was coming, they surrendered and scattered before him; wherever Xi went he won swift victories.

sentences.zh: 永世人徐崇之攻孔景宣，斬之，喜版崇之領縣事。

translations.literal: Xu Chongzhi of Yongshi attacked Kong Jingxuan, beheaded him, and Xi appointed Chongzhi on provisional authority to head county affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chongzhi of Yongshi attacked Kong Jingxuan, beheaded him, and Wu Xi appointed Chongzhi on provisional authority to administer the county.

sentences.zh: 喜至國山，遇東軍，進擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Xi reached Guoshan, encountered the eastern armies, advanced to attack, and routed them thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Xi reached Guoshan, met the eastern army, attacked, and routed it decisively.

sentences.zh: 自國山進屯吳城，劉延熙遣其將楊玄等拒戰。

translations.literal: From Guoshan he advanced to encamp at Wucheng; Liu Yanxi sent his generals Yang Xuan and others to resist in battle.
translations.idiomatic: From Guoshan he advanced to encamp at Wucheng; Liu Yanxi sent his generals Yang Xuan and others to give battle.

sentences.zh: 喜兵力甚弱，玄等眾盛。

translations.literal: Xi's military strength was very weak; Xuan and the others' forces were numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's force was very weak, while Xuan and the others had superior numbers.

sentences.zh: 喜奮擊，斬之，進逼義興。

translations.literal: Xi fought fiercely, beheaded him, and advanced to press Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Xi fought fiercely, beheaded him, and pressed on toward Yixing.

sentences.zh: 延熙柵斷長橋，保郡自守，喜築壘與之相持。

translations.literal: Yanxi palisaded and severed the long bridge, held the commandery and defended himself; Xi built fortifications and faced him in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxi fortified the long bridge, held the commandery, and defended himself; Xi built fortifications and faced him in stalemate.

sentences.zh: 庾業於長塘湖口夾岸築城，有眾七千人，與延熙遙相應接。

translations.literal: Yu Ye built cities on both banks at the mouth of Changtang Lake, had a force of seven thousand men, and coordinated with Yanxi from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ye built fortifications on both banks at the mouth of Changtang Lake with seven thousand men and coordinated with Yanxi from a distance.

sentences.zh: 沈懷明、張永與晉陵軍相持，久不決。

translations.literal: Shen Huaiming, Zhang Yong, and the Jinling army faced each other; for long they could not decide the issue.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huaiming, Zhang Yong, and the Jinling army faced each other for a long time without a decision.

sentences.zh: 外監朱幼舉司徒參軍督護任農夫驍果有膽力，上以四百人配之，使助東討。

translations.literal: Outer Supervisor Zhu You recommended Ren Nongfu, Adjutant and Supervisor of Staff under the Minister over the Masses, as fierce, resolute, and full of daring; the emperor assigned him four hundred men to assist the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Outer supervisor Zhu You recommended staff adjutant Ren Nongfu as fierce and daring; the emperor gave him four hundred men to assist the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 農夫自延陵出長塘，農夫馳往攻之，力戰，大破之，庾業棄城走義興。

translations.literal: Nongfu set out from Yanling toward Changtang; Nongfu galloped to attack; fought fiercely; routed them thoroughly; Yu Ye abandoned the city and fled to Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Nongfu marched from Yanling toward Changtang, galloped to attack, fought fiercely, routed the enemy, and Yu Ye abandoned his fort and fled to Yixing.

sentences.zh: 農夫收其船仗，進向義興，助吳喜。

translations.literal: Nongfu gathered their boats and weapons, advanced toward Yixing, and assisted Wu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Nongfu seized their boats and weapons, advanced on Yixing, and reinforced Wu Xi.

sentences.zh: 二月，己未朔，喜渡水攻郡城，分兵擊諸壘，登高指麾，若令四面俱進者。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the jiwu new moon, Xi crossed the water to attack the commandery city, divided troops to strike the various fortresses, climbed high to command, as if ordering an advance from all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the jiwu new moon, Xi crossed the water to attack the commandery seat, divided his force to strike the outworks, and from high ground directed the battle as though ordering an assault from every side.

sentences.zh: 義興人大懼，諸壘皆潰。

translations.literal: The people of Yixing were greatly afraid; all the fortresses collapsed in flight.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yixing were terrified; every outwork collapsed.

sentences.zh: 延熙赴水死，遂克義興。

translations.literal: Yanxi entered the water and died; they then took Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxi drowned himself; they then took Yixing.

sentences.zh: 魏丞相太原王乙渾專制朝權，多所誅殺。

translations.literal: Northern Wei Chancellor Prince of Taiyuan Yi Hun monopolized court power and put many to death.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei chancellor Prince of Taiyuan Yi Hun monopolized court power and executed many.

sentences.zh: 安遠將軍賈秀掌吏曹事，渾屢言於秀，為其妻求稱公主，秀曰：「公主豈庶姓所宜稱！

translations.literal: Pacifying-the-Distant General Jia Xiu managed the Bureau of Personnel affairs; Hun repeatedly spoke to Xiu, asking that his wife be styled Princess; Xiu said: "How can the title princess suit a base surname!
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying-the-Distant general Jia Xiu ran the personnel bureau; Hun repeatedly pressed Xiu to have his wife styled princess; Xiu said: "How can the title princess suit a common surname!

sentences.zh: 秀寧取死今日，不可取笑後世！」

translations.literal: Xiu would rather die today than become a laughingstock to later ages!"
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die today than become a laughingstock to posterity!"

sentences.zh: 渾怒，罵曰：「老奴官，慳！」

translations.literal: Hun grew angry and cursed: "Old slave official—stingy!"
translations.idiomatic: Hun grew furious and cursed: "Old slave of an official—miser!"

sentences.zh: 會侍中拓跋丕告渾謀反，庚申，馮太后收渾，誅之。

translations.literal: When Attendant-in-Ordinary Tuoba Pi reported that Hun was plotting rebellion, on gengshen Empress Dowager Feng seized Hun and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: When attendant-in-ordinary Tuoba Pi reported Hun's plot to rebel, on gengshen Empress Dowager Feng seized Hun and executed him.

sentences.zh: 秀，彝之子；

translations.literal: Xiu was a son of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was a son of Jia Yi.

sentences.zh: 丕，烈帝之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Pi was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Lie.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Lie.

sentences.zh: 太后臨朝稱制，引中書令高允、中書侍郎漁陽高閭及賈秀共參大政。

translations.literal: The empress dowager held court and assumed the regency; she brought in Secretariat Director Gao Yun, Secretariat Gentleman Gao Lü of Fuyang, and Jia Xiu jointly to deliberate on great affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager held court and assumed the regency, bringing in secretariat director Gao Yun, secretariat gentleman Gao Lü of Fuyang, and Jia Xiu to deliberate on great affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 沈懷明、張永、蕭道成等軍於九里西，與東軍相持。

translations.literal: Shen Huaiming, Zhang Yong, Xiao Daocheng, and others encamped west of Jiuli and faced the eastern army in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huaiming, Zhang Yong, Xiao Daocheng, and others encamped west of Jiuli and faced the eastern army in stalemate.

sentences.zh: 東軍聞義興敗，皆震恐。

translations.literal: The eastern army heard that Yixing had fallen and were all shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern army heard that Yixing had fallen and was shaken with terror.

sentences.zh: 上遣積射將軍濟陽江方興、御史王道隆至晉陵視東軍形勢。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Strongbow General Jiang Fangxing of Jiyang and Censor Wang Daolong to Jinling to observe the eastern army's situation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Strongbow general Jiang Fangxing of Jiyang and censor Wang Daolong to Jinling to reconnoiter the eastern army.

sentences.zh: 孔凱將孫曇扞、程扞宗等列五城，互相連帶。

translations.literal: Kong Kai's generals Sun Tan Guan, Cheng Hanzong, and others arrayed five cities in mutual linkage.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Kai's generals Sun Tan Guan, Cheng Hanzong, and others arrayed five linked strongpoints.

sentences.zh: 扞宗城猶未固，王道隆與諸將謀曰：「扞宗城既未立，可以藉手，上副聖旨，下成眾氣。」

translations.literal: Hanzong's city was not yet secure; Wang Daolong deliberated with the generals: "Since Hanzong's city is not yet established, we may seize the opportunity—above fulfilling the sacred intent, below completing the army's morale."
translations.idiomatic: Hanzong's strongpoint was not yet secure; Wang Daolong said to the generals: "Since Hanzong's position is not yet firm, we can seize the chance—fulfilling the emperor's intent above and steeling the troops below."

sentences.zh: 辛酉，道隆帥所領急攻，拔之，斬扞宗首。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Daolong led those under his command in a swift attack, took it, and beheaded Hanzong.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Daolong led his men in a swift assault, took the place, and beheaded Hanzong.

sentences.zh: 永等因乘勝進擊曇瓘等，壬戌，曇瓘等兵敗，與袁村俱棄城走，遂克晉陵。

translations.literal: Yong and the others then pressed the victory to attack Tan Guan and the others; on renxu, Tan Guan and the others' army was defeated; together with Yuan Village they abandoned the cities and fled; they then took Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong and the others pressed the victory against Tan Guan; on renxu, Tan Guan's force was beaten, abandoned the strongpoints with Yuan Village, and fled; they then took Jinling.

sentences.zh: 吳喜軍至義鄉。

translations.literal: Wu Xi's army reached Yixiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi's army reached Yixiang.

sentences.zh: 孔璪屯吳興南亭，太守王曇生詣璪計事；

translations.literal: Kong Zuan was encamped at Nan Pavilion in Wuxing; Administrator Wang Tansheng went to Zuan to consult on affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Kong Zuan was encamped at Nan Pavilion in Wuxing; administrator Wang Tansheng went to consult with him;

sentences.zh: 聞台軍已近，璪大懼，墮床，曰：「懸賞所購，唯我而已；

translations.literal: on hearing that the court armies were already near, Zuan was greatly afraid, fell from the bed, and said: "The posted reward is offered for me alone;
translations.idiomatic: when he heard the imperial armies were near, Zuan was terrified, fell from his bed, and cried: "The posted reward is for me alone;

sentences.zh: 今不遽走，將為人擒！」

translations.literal: if I do not flee at once, I shall be seized by someone!"
translations.idiomatic: if I do not flee at once, I shall be captured!"

sentences.zh: 遂與曇生奔錢唐。

translations.literal: He then fled with Tansheng to Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: He fled with Tansheng to Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 喜入吳興，任農夫引兵向吳郡，顧琛棄郡奔會稽。

translations.literal: Xi entered Wuxing; Ren Nongfu led troops toward Wu Commandery; Gu Chen abandoned the commandery and fled to Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Xi entered Wuxing; Ren Nongfu led troops toward Wu Commandery; Gu Chen abandoned the seat and fled to Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 上以四郡既平，乃留吳喜使統沈懷明等諸將東擊會稽，召張永等北擊彭城，江方興等南擊尋陽。

translations.literal: Since the four commanderies were already pacified, the emperor retained Wu Xi to command Shen Huaiming and the other generals in an eastern strike on Kuaiji, summoned Zhang Yong and others north to attack Pengcheng, and Jiang Fangxing and others south to attack Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: With the four commanderies pacified, the emperor kept Wu Xi to command Shen Huaiming and the others east against Kuaiji, recalled Zhang Yong north against Pengcheng, and sent Jiang Fangxing south against Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 以吏部尚書蔡興宗為左僕射，侍中褚淵為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He appointed Minister of Personnel Cai Xingzong Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Attendant-in-Ordinary Chu Yuan Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Minister of Personnel Cai Xingzong left vice director of the Imperial Secretariat and attendant-in-ordinary Chu Yuan minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，吳喜至錢唐，孔璪、王曇生奔浙東。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Wu Xi reached Qiantang; Kong Zuan and Wang Tansheng fled to eastern Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Wu Xi reached Qiantang; Kong Zuan and Wang Tansheng fled into eastern Zhe.

sentences.zh: 喜遣強弩將軍任農夫等引兵向黃山浦；

translations.literal: Xi sent Strong Crossbow General Ren Nongfu and others to lead troops toward Huangshan Ford;
translations.idiomatic: Xi sent Strong Crossbow general Ren Nongfu and others toward Huangshan Ford;

sentences.zh: 東軍據岸結寨，農夫等擊破之。

translations.literal: the eastern army held the bank and built stockades; Nongfu and the others attacked and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: the eastern army held the bank and built stockades; Nongfu and his men attacked and broke them.

sentences.zh: 喜自柳浦渡，取西陵，擊斬庚業。

translations.literal: Xi crossed from Liupu, took Xiling, and attacked and beheaded Geng Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Xi crossed from Liupu, took Xiling, and attacked and beheaded Geng Ye.

sentences.zh: 會稽人大懼，將士多奔亡，孔凱不能制。

translations.literal: The people of Kuaiji were greatly afraid; officers and soldiers mostly fled; Kong Kai could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Kuaiji were terrified; officers and soldiers fled in droves; Kong Kai could not control them.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，上虞令王晏起兵攻郡，凱逃奔脊山；

translations.literal: On wuyin, Shangyu magistrate Wang Yan raised troops to attack the commandery; Kai fled to Jishan;
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Shangyu magistrate Wang Yan raised troops against the commandery; Kong Kai fled to Jishan;

sentences.zh: 車騎從事中郎張綏封府庫以待吳喜。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk to the General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Sui sealed the government treasury to await Wu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk to the general of chariots and cavalry Zhang Sui sealed the government treasury to await Wu Xi.

sentences.zh: 己卯，王晏入城，殺綏，執尋陽王子房於別署。

translations.literal: On jimao, Wang Yan entered the city, killed Sui, and seized Prince of Xunyang Zifang at a separate residence.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Wang Yan entered the city, killed Zhang Sui, and seized Prince of Xunyang Liu Zifang at a separate residence.

sentences.zh: 縱兵大掠，府庫皆空；

translations.literal: He let the troops plunder freely; the treasury was emptied;
translations.idiomatic: He let his troops plunder freely; the treasury was emptied;

sentences.zh: 獲孔璪，殺之。

translations.literal: they captured Kong Zuan and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: they captured Kong Zuan and killed him.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，脊山民縛孔凱送晏，晏謂之曰：「此事孔璪所為，無預卿事，可作首辭，當相為申上。」

translations.literal: On gengchen, the people of Jishan bound Kong Kai and sent him to Yan; Yan said to him: "This affair was Kong Zuan's doing; it does not involve you; you may compose a memorial of confession and I shall present it on your behalf to the throne."
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, the people of Jishan bound Kong Kai and sent him to Wang Yan; Yan said to him: "This was Kong Zuan's doing and does not involve you; draft a confession and I will present it for you at court."

sentences.zh: 凱曰：「江東處分，莫不由身；

translations.literal: Kai said: "Every disposition in Jiangdong was none other than my own;
translations.idiomatic: Kong Kai said: "Every decision in the Jiangdong region was mine alone;

sentences.zh: 委罪求活，便是君輩行意耳。」

translations.literal: to shift blame to seek life—that is precisely your sort's intent."
translations.idiomatic: to shift blame to save my skin—that is exactly your sort's way."

sentences.zh: 晏乃斬之。

translations.literal: Yan then beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 顧琛、王曇生、袁標等詣吳喜歸罪，喜皆宥之。

translations.literal: Gu Chen, Wang Tansheng, Yuan Biao, and others came to Wu Xi to surrender blame; Xi pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Chen, Wang Tansheng, Yuan Biao, and others came to Wu Xi to surrender; Xi pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 東軍主凡七十六人，於陳斬十七人，其餘皆原宥。

translations.literal: Eastern army commanders numbered seventy-six in all; seventeen were beheaded in the array; the rest were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Of seventy-six eastern army commanders in all, seventeen were beheaded in battle; the rest were all pardoned.

sentences.zh: 薛索兒攻申闡，久不下；

translations.literal: Xue Suo'er attacked Shen Chan; for long he could not take him down;
translations.idiomatic: Xue Suo'er besieged Shen Chan for a long time without success;

sentences.zh: 使申令孫入睢陵說闡，闡出降，索兒並令孫殺之。

translations.literal: he sent Shen Lingsun into Suiling to persuade Chan; Chan came out to surrender; Suo'er killed both Chan and Lingsun.
translations.idiomatic: he sent Shen Lingsun into Suiling to persuade Chan; Chan came out to surrender; Suo'er had both Chan and Lingsun killed.

sentences.zh: 山陽王休祐在歷陽，輔國將軍劉勉進軍小峴。

translations.literal: Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was at Liyang; Supporting-the-State General Liu Mian advanced the army to Xiaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shanyang Liu Xiuyou was at Liyang; Supporting-the-State general Liu Mian advanced to Xiaoxian.

sentences.zh: 殷琰所署南汝陰太守裴季之以合肥來降。

translations.literal: Pei Jizhi, whom Yin Yan had appointed Administrator of Southern Runan, came from Hefei to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Jizhi, whom Yin Yan had appointed southern Runan administrator, came from Hefei to surrender.

sentences.zh: 鄧琬性鄙暗貪吝，既執大權，父子賣官鬻爵，使婢僕出市道販賣；

translations.literal: Deng Wan by nature was vulgar, obtuse, and greedy; once he grasped great power, father and son sold offices and peddled noble ranks and sent maidservants and servants out to hawk goods in the markets;
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan was vulgar, obtuse, and greedy by nature; once he held supreme power, father and son sold offices and titles and sent maids and servants to hawk goods in the streets;

sentences.zh: 酣歌博弈，日夜不休；

translations.literal: they caroused, sang, played games, and gambled night and day without cease;
translations.idiomatic: they feasted, sang, and gambled night and day without cease;

sentences.zh: 大自矜遇，賓客到門，歷旬不得前；

translations.literal: he greatly indulged his own consequence; when guests came to his gate, for whole ten-day periods they could not gain access;
translations.idiomatic: he indulged his own importance; guests who came to his gate might wait ten days without admission;

sentences.zh: 內事悉委褚靈嗣等三人，群小橫恣，競為威福。

translations.literal: internal affairs were wholly entrusted to Chu Lingsi and three others; petty men ran riot and vied to wield authority and favor.
translations.idiomatic: he entrusted internal affairs entirely to Chu Lingsi and two others; petty men ran riot and vied for power and favor.

sentences.zh: 於是士民仇怨，內外離心。

translations.literal: Thereupon scholars and commoners bore hatred; within and without hearts turned away.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners turned hostile; the regime lost heart within and without.

sentences.zh: 琬遣孫沖帥龍驤將軍薛常寶、陳紹宗、焦度等兵一萬為前鋒，據赭圻。

translations.literal: Wan sent Sun Chong to lead Dragon-Prancing General Xue Changbao, Chen Shaozong, Jiao Du, and others with ten thousand troops as vanguard to hold Zhitu.
translations.idiomatic: Wan sent Sun Chong at the head of Dragon-Prancing general Xue Changbao, Chen Shaozong, Jiao Du, and ten thousand men as vanguard to hold Zhitu.

sentences.zh: 沖之於道與晉安王子勳書曰：「舟楫已辦，器械亦整，三軍踴躍，人爭效命；

translations.literal: On the road Chong wrote to Prince of Jin'an Zixun: "Boats and oars are ready, weapons and gear are also in order, the three armies leap with zeal, and men vie to offer their lives;
translations.idiomatic: On the march Chong wrote to Prince of Jin'an Liu Zixun: "The fleet is ready and the weapons in order; the three armies are eager and every man vies to give his life;

sentences.zh: 便欲沿流掛帆，直取白下。

translations.literal: we wish at once to sail with the current, hoist the sails, and strike straight for Baixia.
translations.idiomatic: we mean to run downstream under full sail and strike straight for Baixia.

sentences.zh: 願速遣陶亮眾軍兼行相接，分據新亭、南州，則一麾定矣。」

translations.literal: I pray you speedily dispatch Tao Liang's hosts to march in parallel and link up, and seize Xinting and Nanzhou in division—then one wave of the banner will settle all."
translations.idiomatic: Send Tao Liang's army at once to march in parallel and join us, seize Xinting and Nanzhou between us, and the matter will be settled with a single command."

sentences.zh: 子勳加沖左衛將軍；

translations.literal: Zixun promoted Chong to Left Guard General;
translations.idiomatic: Zixun promoted Chong to left guard general;

sentences.zh: 以陶亮變右衛將軍，統郢、荊、湘、梁、雍五州兵合二萬人，一時俱下。

translations.literal: he made Tao Liang acting Right Guard General, commanding troops of the five provinces Ying, Jing, Xiang, Liang, and Yong totaling twenty thousand men, all to descend together at one time.
translations.idiomatic: he made Tao Liang acting right guard general, commanding twenty thousand troops from Ying, Jing, Xiang, Liang, and Yong to descend together at once.

sentences.zh: 陶亮本無干略，聞建安王休仁自上，殷孝祖又至，不敢進，屯軍鵲洲。

translations.literal: Tao Liang was by nature without capacity for strategy; on hearing that Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was coming down from above and Yin Xiaozu had also arrived, he did not dare advance and encamped at Quezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Liang had no real strategic talent; when he heard that Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren was coming downriver and Yin Xiaozu had also arrived, he did not dare advance and encamped at Quezhou.

sentences.zh: 殷孝祖負其誠節，陵轢諸將，台軍有父子兄弟在南者，孝祖悉欲推治。

translations.literal: Yin Xiaozu relied on his loyal integrity, bullied the generals, and whenever court troops had fathers, sons, or brothers in the south, Xiaozu wished to investigate and punish them all.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Xiaozu took pride in his loyal integrity, bullied the other generals, and wanted to prosecute every imperial soldier who had fathers, sons, or brothers in the rebel south.

sentences.zh: 由是人情乖離，莫樂為用。

translations.literal: Hence human hearts turned estranged; none were willing to serve gladly.
translations.idiomatic: Morale collapsed; no one was willing to fight wholeheartedly for him.

sentences.zh: 寧朔將軍沈攸之，內撫將士，外諧群帥，眾並賴之。

translations.literal: Pacifying-the-North General Shen Youzhi inwardly comforted officers and soldiers and outwardly harmonized with the collective commanders; all relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying-the-North general Shen Youzhi comforted the troops within and worked harmoniously with the other commanders; everyone relied on him.

sentences.zh: 孝祖每戰，常以鼓蓋自隨，軍中人相謂：「殷統軍可謂死將矣！

translations.literal: Whenever Xiaozu fought, he always had drum covers accompany him; men in the army said to one another: "Commander Yin may be called a dead general!
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Xiaozu went into battle he had ceremonial drum covers carried before him; the men in camp said to one another: "Commander Yin is a dead man walking!

sentences.zh: 今與賊交鋒，而以羽儀自標顯，若善射者十人共射之，欲不斃，得乎？」

translations.literal: Now he crosses spears with the enemy yet displays ceremonial regalia to mark himself out—if ten skilled archers shot at him together, how could he fail to fall?"
translations.idiomatic: He is crossing spears with the enemy yet parades his ceremonial regalia—if ten good archers shot at him together, how could he fail to fall?"

sentences.zh: 三月，庚寅，眾軍水陸並進，攻赭圻；

translations.literal: In the third month, on gengyin, the massed armies advanced by land and water together and attacked Zhitu;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengyin, the combined armies advanced by land and water against Zhitu;

sentences.zh: 陶亮等引兵救之，孝祖於陳為流矢所中，死。

translations.literal: Tao Liang and others led troops to relieve them; Xiaozu was struck in battle by a stray arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Liang and others led troops to the rescue; Yin Xiaozu was struck by a stray arrow in the fighting and died.

sentences.zh: 軍主范潛帥五百人降於亮。

translations.literal: Army commander Fan Qian led five hundred men in surrender to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Army commander Fan Qian led five hundred men in surrender to Tao Liang.

sentences.zh: 人情震駭，並謂沈攸之宜代孝祖為統。

translations.literal: Popular sentiment was shaken, and all said Shen Youzhi ought to replace Xiaozu as commander.
translations.idiomatic: Hearts were shaken throughout the army, and all said Shen Youzhi ought to replace Xiaozu as overall commander.

sentences.zh: 時建安王休仁屯虎檻，遣寧朔將軍江方興、龍驤將軍襄陽劉靈遺各將三千人赴赭圻。

translations.literal: At this time Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren was encamped at Hujian and sent Pacifying-the-North general Jiang Fangxing and Dragon-Coursing general Liu Lingyi of Xiangyang, each with three thousand men, to Zhitu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren was then encamped at Hujian and sent Pacifying-the-North general Jiang Fangxing and Dragon-Coursing general Liu Lingyi of Xiangyang, each leading three thousand men, toward Zhitu.

sentences.zh: 攸之以為孝祖既死，亮等有乘勝之心，明日若不更攻，則示之以弱。

translations.literal: Youzhi held that with Xiaozu dead, Liang and the others would have the mind to press their victory; if they did not attack again tomorrow, it would show weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi reasoned that with Xiaozu dead, Liang and the others would be eager to press their victory; if the army did not attack again the next day, it would signal weakness.

sentences.zh: 方興各位相亞，必不為己下；

translations.literal: Fangxing and the others were of equal rank and would certainly not serve under him;
translations.idiomatic: Fangxing and the others were his equals in rank and would never take orders from him;

sentences.zh: 軍政不壹，致敗之由也。

translations.literal: with military authority not unified, that was the cause of defeat.
translations.idiomatic: when military authority is divided, that is how armies are defeated.

sentences.zh: 乃帥諸軍主詣方興曰：「今四方並反，國家所保，無復百里之地。

translations.literal: He therefore led the army commanders to Fangxing and said: "Now the four quarters have all rebelled; what the state still holds is no more than a hundred li of territory.
translations.idiomatic: He led the army commanders to Fangxing and said: "The four quarters have all risen in rebellion; the realm retains scarcely a hundred li of territory.

sentences.zh: 唯有殷孝祖為朝廷所委賴，鋒鏑裁交，輿屍而反，文武喪氣，朝野危心。

translations.literal: Only Yin Xiaozu was entrusted by the court; blades had scarcely crossed when his corpse was brought back in the carriage; civil and military men lost heart, and court and realm stood in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yin Xiaozu was the court's mainstay; blades had scarcely crossed when his corpse was brought back; civil and military men lost heart, and court and realm stood in peril.

sentences.zh: 事之濟否，唯在時旦一戰；

translations.literal: Whether affairs succeed depends on one battle fought at once;
translations.idiomatic: Whether we prevail depends on a single battle fought at once;

sentences.zh: 戰若不捷，則大事去矣。

translations.literal: if the battle is not won, the great enterprise is lost.
translations.idiomatic: if we do not win, the great enterprise is lost.

sentences.zh: 詰朝之事，諸人或謂吾應統之，自卜懦薄，干略不如卿。

translations.literal: As for tomorrow's affair, some may say I ought to take command; judging myself timid and slight, my planning and resolve are not equal to yours.
translations.idiomatic: As for tomorrow, some may say I ought to take command; I know myself timid and slight, and my planning is not equal to yours.

sentences.zh: 今輒相推為統，但當相與戮力耳。」

translations.literal: I now press command upon you; we need only exert our strength together."
translations.idiomatic: I now yield command to you; we need only fight together with all our strength."

sentences.zh: 方興甚悅，許諾。

translations.literal: Fangxing was greatly pleased and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Fangxing was greatly pleased and agreed.

sentences.zh: 攸之既出，諸軍主並尤之，攸之曰：「吾本以濟國活家，豈計此之升降！

translations.literal: After Youzhi had gone out, the army commanders all blamed him; Youzhi said: "I mean to save the state and preserve our houses—how could I calculate such rise and fall!
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhi had gone out, the commanders all blamed him; Youzhi said: "I mean to save the state and our families—why should I calculate rank and precedence!

sentences.zh: 且我能下彼，彼必不能下我。

translations.literal: Moreover, I can yield to them; they certainly cannot yield to me.
translations.idiomatic: I can yield to them; they cannot yield to me.

sentences.zh: 共濟艱難，豈可自措同異也！」

translations.literal: To endure hardship together—how can we indulge private differences!"
translations.idiomatic: To endure hardship together—how can we indulge private differences!"

sentences.zh: 孫沖之謂陶亮曰：「孝祖梟將，一戰便死，天下事定矣，不須復戰，便當直取京都。」

translations.literal: Sun Chong wrote to Tao Liang: "Xiaozu was a fierce general; he died in a single battle; the empire is settled—no need to fight again; we should march straight on the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chong wrote to Tao Liang: "Xiaozu was a fierce general; one battle killed him; the empire is settled—no need to fight again; we should sail straight for the capital."

sentences.zh: 亮不從。

translations.literal: Liang would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Liang would not listen.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，方興帥諸軍進戰，建安王休仁又遣軍主郭季之、步兵校尉杜幼文、屯騎校尉垣恭祖、龍驤將軍濟地頓生京兆段佛榮等三萬人往會戰，自寅及午，大破之，追奔至姥山而還。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Fangxing led the armies into battle; Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren also sent army commander Guo Jizhi, Infantry Commandant Du Youwen, Commandant of Palace Steeds Yuan Gongzu, Dragon-Coursing general Duan Furong of Jingzhao in Jidi, and others with thirty thousand men to join the fight; from yin through wu they won a great victory and pursued the fugitives to Laoshan before returning.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Fangxing led the armies into battle; Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren also sent army commander Guo Jizhi, Infantry Commandant Du Youwen, Commandant of Palace Steeds Yuan Gongzu, Dragon-Coursing general Duan Furong of Jingzhao in Jidi, and thirty thousand others to join the fight; from dawn through noon they won a great victory and pursued the fugitives to Laoshan before returning.

sentences.zh: 幼文，驥之子也。

translations.literal: Youwen was the son of Du Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Youwen was the son of Du Ji.

sentences.zh: 孫沖子於湖、白口築二城，軍主竟陵張興世攻拔之。

translations.literal: Sun Chong's son built two strongpoints at Hu and Baikou; army commander Zhang Xingshi of Jingling attacked and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chong's son built two strongpoints at Hu and Baikou; army commander Zhang Xingshi of Jingling attacked and captured them.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，詔以沈攸之為輔國將軍、假節，代殷孝祖督前鋒諸軍事。

translations.literal: On renchen, an edict appointed Shen Youzhi Supporting-the-State general with provisional credentials, replacing Yin Xiaozu in command of all vanguard forces.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, an edict appointed Shen Youzhi Supporting-the-State general with provisional credentials, replacing Yin Xiaozu as commander of all vanguard forces.

sentences.zh: 陶亮聞湖、白二城不守，大懼，急召孫沖之還鵲尾，留薛常寶等守赭圻；

translations.literal: When Tao Liang heard that Hu and Baikou had fallen, he was greatly afraid and urgently summoned Sun Chong back to Quewei, leaving Xue Changbao and others to hold Zhitu;
translations.idiomatic: When Tao Liang heard that Hu and Baikou had fallen, he was terrified and urgently summoned Sun Chong back to Quewei, leaving Xue Changbao and others to hold Zhitu;

sentences.zh: 先於姥山及諸岡分立營寨，亦悉散還，共保濃湖。

translations.literal: the camps he had first set up on Laoshan and the various hillocks were all abandoned as well, and all withdrew together to defend Nonghu.
translations.idiomatic: the camps on Laoshan and the various hillocks were all abandoned, and everyone withdrew to defend Nonghu together.

sentences.zh: 時軍旅大起，國用不足，募民上錢穀者，賜荒縣、荒郡，或五品至三品散官有差。

translations.literal: At this time armies were raised on a great scale and state revenues were insufficient; those who contributed money and grain were rewarded with barren counties and commanderies, or with honorary offices from fifth to third rank according to amount.
translations.idiomatic: Armies were raised on a vast scale and state revenues ran short; those who contributed money and grain were rewarded with barren counties and commanderies, or honorary offices from fifth to third rank according to amount.

sentences.zh: 軍中食少，建安王休仁撫循將士，均其豐儉，吊死問傷，身親隱恤；

translations.literal: Food in the army was scarce; Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren comforted and led the soldiers, equalizing plenty and want among them, mourning the dead and asking after the wounded, personally showing hidden care;
translations.idiomatic: Food in the army was scarce; Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren comforted the troops, equalizing plenty and want, mourning the dead and asking after the wounded, personally showing care in secret;

sentences.zh: 故十萬之眾，莫有離心。

translations.literal: therefore among his force of a hundred thousand none had a mind to depart.
translations.idiomatic: and so among his hundred thousand men none had a mind to depart.

sentences.zh: 鄧琬遣其豫州刺史劉胡帥眾三萬、鐵騎二千，東屯鵲尾，並舊兵凡十餘萬。

translations.literal: Deng Wan sent his Inspector of Yuzhou Liu Hu east with thirty thousand men and two thousand armored horsemen to encamp at Quewei, together with the old troops more than a hundred thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan sent his Yuzhou inspector Liu Hu east with thirty thousand men and two thousand armored horsemen to encamp at Quewei, and with the old troops the force exceeded a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 胡，宿將，勇健多權略，屢有戰功，將士畏之。

translations.literal: Hu was a veteran general, brave, hardy, and full of stratagems, with repeated battle achievements; officers and soldiers feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Hu was a veteran general, brave, hardy, and resourceful, with many battle honors; officers and soldiers feared him.

sentences.zh: 司徒中兵參軍冠軍蔡那，子弟在襄陽，胡每戰，懸之城外；

translations.literal: Staff Officer for the Central Troops Cai Na of the Champions, whose younger kinsmen were in Xiangyang, had them hung outside the walls whenever Hu fought;
translations.idiomatic: Staff Officer for the Central Troops Cai Na of the Champions, whose younger kinsmen were in Xiangyang, had them hung outside the walls whenever Hu fought;

sentences.zh: 那進戰不顧。

translations.literal: Na advanced to battle without regard.
translations.idiomatic: Na advanced to battle without regard.

sentences.zh: 吳喜既定三吳，帥所領五千人，並運資實，至於赭圻。

translations.literal: After Wu Xi had pacified the three Wu regions, he led his five thousand men and also transported supplies and goods to Zhitu.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Xi had pacified the three Wu regions, he led his five thousand men and transported supplies and goods to Zhitu.

sentences.zh: 薛索兒將馬步萬餘人自睢陵渡淮，進逼青、冀二州刺史張永營。

translations.literal: Xue Suo'er led more than ten thousand horse and foot from Suiling across the Huai, pressing upon the camp of Zhang Yong, Inspector of Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Suo'er led more than ten thousand horse and foot from Suiling across the Huai and pressed upon the camp of Qing and Ji inspector Zhang Yong.

sentences.zh: 丙申，詔南徐州刺史桂陽王休范統北討諸軍事，進據廣陵；

translations.literal: On bingshen, an edict made Prince of Guiyang Liu Xiufan overall commander of the northern punitive armies and ordered him to advance and hold Guangling;
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, an edict made Prince of Guiyang Liu Xiufan overall commander of the northern punitive armies and ordered him to advance and hold Guangling;

sentences.zh: 又詔蕭道成將兵救永。

translations.literal: another edict ordered Xiao Daocheng to lead troops to rescue Yong.
translations.idiomatic: another edict ordered Xiao Daocheng to lead troops to rescue Zhang Yong.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，尋陽王子房至建康，上宥之，貶爵為松滋侯。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Prince of Xunyang Liu Zifang reached Jiankang; the emperor pardoned him and reduced his noble rank to Marquis of Songzi.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Prince of Xunyang Liu Zifang reached Jiankang; the emperor pardoned him and reduced his noble rank to Marquis of Songzi.

sentences.zh: 庚子，魏以陝西王源賀為太尉。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Wei appointed Wang Yuanhe of Shaanxi Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Northern Wei appointed Wang Yuanhe of Shaanxi Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 上遣寧朔將軍劉懷珍帥龍驤將軍王敬則等步騎五千，助劉勉討壽陽，斬廬江太守劉道蔚。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Pacifying-the-North general Liu Huaizhen with Dragon-Coursing general Wang Jingze and others, five thousand foot and horse, to assist Liu Mian in attacking Shouyang and beheaded Liu Daowei, Prefect of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Pacifying-the-North general Liu Huaizhen with Dragon-Coursing general Wang Jingze and five thousand foot and horse to assist Liu Mian against Shouyang and beheaded Lujiang prefect Liu Daowei.

sentences.zh: 懷珍，善明之從子也。

translations.literal: Huaizhen was a nephew of Liu Shanming.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen was a nephew of Liu Shanming.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人戴明寶啟上，遣軍主竟陵黃回募兵擊斬尋陽所署馬頭太守王廣元。

translations.literal: Central Palace Gentleman Dai Mingbao memorialized the throne; the emperor sent army commander Huang Hui of Jingling to recruit troops, attack, and behead Wang Guangyuan, whom Xunyang had appointed Prefect of Matou.
translations.idiomatic: Central palace gentleman Dai Mingbao memorialized the throne; the emperor sent army commander Huang Hui of Jingling to recruit troops, attack, and behead Wang Guangyuan, whom Xunyang had appointed Matou prefect.

sentences.zh: 前奉朝請壽陽鄭黑，起兵於淮上以應建康，東扞殷琰，西拒常珍奇；

translations.literal: Former Court Gentleman Zheng Hei of Shouyang raised troops on the Huai in support of Jiankang, holding the east against Yin Yan and the west against Chang Zhenqi;
translations.idiomatic: Former court gentleman Zheng Hei of Shouyang raised troops on the Huai for Jiankang, holding the east against Yin Yan and the west against Chang Zhenqi;

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以黑為司州刺史。

translations.literal: on yisi he was appointed Inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: on yisi he was appointed Sizhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 殷琰將劉順、柳倫、皇甫道烈、龐天生等馬步八千人東據宛唐；

translations.literal: Yin Yan's generals Liu Shun, Liu Lun, Huangfu Daolie, Pang Tiansheng, and others, eight thousand horse and foot, held Wantang in the east;
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yan's generals Liu Shun, Liu Lun, Huangfu Daolie, Pang Tiansheng, and others—eight thousand horse and foot—held Wantang in the east;

sentences.zh: 劉勉帥眾軍並進，去順數里立營。

translations.literal: Liu Mian led the armies forward together and encamped several li from Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian led all the armies forward and encamped several li from Shun.

sentences.zh: 時琰所遣諸軍，並受順節度，而以皇甫道烈土豪，柳倫台之所遣，順本卑微，唯不使經督二軍。

translations.literal: At that time all the armies Yan had sent were under Shun's command, but because Huangfu Daolie was a local strongman and Liu Lun had been sent by the court, Shun was originally low in standing and was not allowed to oversee the other two armies.
translations.idiomatic: All the armies Yan had sent were nominally under Shun's command, but because Huangfu Daolie was a local strongman and Liu Lun had been sent by the court, Shun was low in standing and was not allowed to oversee the other two armies.

sentences.zh: 勉始至，塹壘未立；

translations.literal: When Mian had just arrived, trenches and ramparts were not yet set;
translations.idiomatic: When Mian had just arrived, trenches and ramparts were not yet built;

sentences.zh: 順欲擊之，道烈，倫不同，順不能獨進，乃止。

translations.literal: Shun wished to attack, but Daolie and Lun disagreed; Shun could not advance alone and therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shun wished to attack, but Daolie and Lun disagreed; Shun could not advance alone and held back.

sentences.zh: 勉營既立，不可復攻，因相持守。

translations.literal: Once Mian's camp was established, he could not attack again, and the two sides settled into a stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: Once Mian's camp was established, attack was no longer possible, and the two sides settled into a stalemate.

sentences.zh: 壬子，斷新錢，專用古錢。

translations.literal: On renzi, new coin was abolished and only old coin was used.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, new coin was abolished and only old coin was permitted.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之帥諸軍圍赭圻。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi led the armies in besieging Zhitu.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi led the armies in besieging Zhitu.

sentences.zh: 薛常寶等糧盡，告劉胡求救；

translations.literal: When Xue Changbao and the others ran out of grain, they asked Liu Hu for rescue;
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Changbao and the others ran out of grain, they asked Liu Hu for rescue;

sentences.zh: 胡以囊盛米，系流查及船腹，陽覆船，順風流下以餉之。
