translations.literal: Hu put rice in bags, tied them to floating logs and the bellies of boats, capsized the boats in appearance, and sent them downstream with the wind to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Hu put rice in bags, tied them to floating logs and the undersides of boats, feigned capsized boats, and sent them downstream with the wind as supplies.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之疑其有異，遣人取船及流查，大得囊米。

translations.literal: Youzhi suspected something unusual, sent men to take the boats and floating logs, and recovered a great quantity of bagged rice.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi suspected a trick, sent men to recover the boats and logs, and found a great quantity of bagged rice.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，劉胡帥步卒一萬，夜，斫山開道，以布囊運米餉赭圻。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Liu Hu led ten thousand foot soldiers by night, cut through the mountains to open a road, and transported rice in cloth bags to supply Zhitu.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Liu Hu led ten thousand foot soldiers by night, cut through the mountains to open a road, and transported rice in cloth bags to supply Zhitu.

sentences.zh: 平旦，至城下，猶隔小塹，未能入。

translations.literal: At dawn they reached below the walls but were still separated by a small moat and could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they reached below the walls but were still separated by a small moat and could not enter.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之帥諸軍邀之，殊死戰，胡眾大敗，捨糧棄甲，緣山走，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Youzhi led the armies to intercept them; they fought to the death; Hu's force was greatly defeated, abandoned grain and armor, and fled along the mountains; the slain and captured were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi led the armies to intercept them; they fought to the death; Hu's force was routed, abandoned grain and armor, and fled along the mountains; the slain and captured were very many.

sentences.zh: 胡被瘡，僅得還營。

translations.literal: Hu was wounded and barely made it back to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Hu was wounded and barely made it back to camp.

sentences.zh: 常寶等惶懼，夏，四月，辛酉，開城突圍，走還胡軍。

translations.literal: Changbao and the others were terrified; in summer, the fourth month, on xinyou, they opened the city and broke out, fleeing back to Hu's army.
translations.idiomatic: Changbao and the others were terrified; in summer, the fourth month, on xinyou, they opened the city, broke out, and fled back to Hu's army.

sentences.zh: 攸之拔赭圻城，斬其寧朔將軍沈懷寶等，納降數千人。

translations.literal: Youzhi took Zhitu, beheaded Pacifying-the-North general Shen Huaibao and others, and accepted several thousand surrenders.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi took Zhitu, beheaded Pacifying-the-North general Shen Huaibao and others, and accepted several thousand surrenders.

sentences.zh: 陳紹宗單舸奔鵲尾。

translations.literal: Chen Shaozong fled alone in a single boat to Quewei.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaozong fled alone in a single boat to Quewei.

sentences.zh: 建安王休仁自虎檻進屯赭圻。

translations.literal: Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren advanced from Hujian and encamped at Zhitu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren advanced from Hujian and encamped at Zhitu.

sentences.zh: 劉胡等兵猶盛。

translations.literal: Liu Hu and the others still had a strong army.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu and the others still commanded a strong army.

sentences.zh: 上欲綏慰人情，遣吏部尚書褚淵至虎檻，選用將士。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to soothe popular sentiment and sent Minister of Personnel Chu Yuan to Hujian to select and appoint officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to soothe hearts and sent Minister of Personnel Chu Yuan to Hujian to select and appoint officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 時以軍功除官者眾，版不能供，始用黃紙。

translations.literal: At this time so many were ennobled for military merit that the printing blocks could not supply them, and yellow paper began to be used.
translations.idiomatic: So many were ennobled for military merit that the printing blocks could not supply the commissions, and yellow paper began to be used.

sentences.zh: 鄧琬以晉安王子勳之命，征袁顗下尋陽，顗悉雍州之眾馳下。

translations.literal: By order of Prince of Jin'an Liu Zixun, Deng Wan summoned Yuan Yi down from Xunyang, and Yi galloped down with all the forces of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By order of Prince of Jin'an Liu Zixun, Deng Wan summoned Yuan Yi down from Xunyang, and Yi galloped down with all the forces of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 琬以黃門侍郎劉道憲行荊州事。

translations.literal: Wan appointed Palace Attendant Liu Daoxian acting Administrator of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wan appointed palace attendant Liu Daoxian acting Jingzhou administrator.

sentences.zh: 侍中孔道存行雍州事。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-ordinary Kong Daocun was made acting Administrator of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-ordinary Kong Daocun was made acting Yongzhou administrator.

sentences.zh: 上庸太守柳世隆乘虛襲襄陽，不克。

translations.literal: Liu Shilong, Prefect of Shangyong, seized the moment to strike Xiangyang but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyong prefect Liu Shilong seized the moment to strike Xiangyang but did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 世隆，元景之弟子也。

translations.literal: Shilong was a nephew of Liu Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong was a nephew of Liu Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 散騎侍郎明僧暠為青州刺史。

translations.literal: Gentleman for Miscellaneous Uses Ming Seng'ao was appointed Inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman for Miscellaneous Uses Ming Seng'ao was appointed Qingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 平原、樂安二郡太守王玄默據琅邪，清河、廣川二郡太守王玄邈據盤陽城，高陽、勃海二郡太守劉乘民據臨濟城，並起兵以應建康。

translations.literal: Wang Xuanmo, joint Prefect of Pingyuan and Le'an, held Langye; Wang Xuanmiao, joint Prefect of Qinghe and Guangchuan, held Panyang; Liu Chenmin, joint Prefect of Gaoyang and Bohai, held Linji—all raised troops in support of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanmo, joint prefect of Pingyuan and Le'an, held Langye; Wang Xuanmiao, joint prefect of Qinghe and Guangchuan, held Panyang; Liu Chenmin, joint prefect of Gaoyang and Bohai, held Linji—all raised troops for Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 玄邈，玄謨之從弟；

translations.literal: Xuanmiao was a younger cousin of Xuanmo;
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmiao was a younger cousin of Wang Xuanmo;

sentences.zh: 乘民，彌之之從子也。

translations.literal: Chenmin was a nephew of Mizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Chenmin was a nephew of Liu Mizhi.

sentences.zh: 沈文秀遣軍主解彥士攻北海，拔之，殺劉彌之。

translations.literal: Shen Wenxiu sent army commander Xie Yanshi to attack Beihai, captured it, and killed Liu Mizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Wenxiu sent army commander Xie Yanshi to attack Beihai, captured it, and killed Liu Mizhi.

sentences.zh: 乘民從弟伯宗，合帥鄉黨，復取北海，因引兵向青州所治東陽城。

translations.literal: Chenmin's younger cousin Bozong gathered the village clans, recovered Beihai, and then led troops toward Dongyang, where the Qingzhou government was seated.
translations.idiomatic: Chenmin's younger cousin Bozong gathered the village clans, recovered Beihai, and marched toward Dongyang, seat of the Qingzhou government.

sentences.zh: 文秀拒之，伯宗戰死。

translations.literal: Wenxiu resisted him; Bozong died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu resisted him; Bozong died in battle.

sentences.zh: 僧暠、玄默、玄邈、乘民合兵攻東陽城，每戰，輒為文秀所破，離而復合，如此者十餘，卒不能克。

translations.literal: Seng'ao, Xuanmo, Xuanmiao, and Chenmin combined forces to attack Dongyang; in every battle they were beaten by Wenxiu; they separated and rejoined more than ten times and ultimately could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Seng'ao, Xuanmo, Xuanmiao, and Chenmin combined to attack Dongyang; in every battle Wenxiu defeated them; they broke apart and rejoined more than ten times and ultimately could not take the city.

sentences.zh: 杜淑寶謂台軍住歷陽，不能遽進；

translations.literal: Du Shubao held that the imperial armies were stationed at Liyang and could not advance quickly;
translations.idiomatic: Du Shubao held that the imperial armies were at Liyang and could not advance quickly;

sentences.zh: 及劉勉等至，上下震恐。

translations.literal: when Liu Mian and the others arrived, high and low were all terrified.
translations.idiomatic: when Liu Mian and the others arrived, everyone was terrified.

sentences.zh: 劉順等始行，唯繼一月糧，既與勉久相持，糧盡。

translations.literal: When Shun and the others had first set out, they had only one month's rations; after a long stalemate with Mian, the grain was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun had first set out, he had only one month's rations; after a long stalemate with Mian, the grain ran out.

sentences.zh: 叔寶發車千五百乘，載米餉順，自將五千精兵送之。

translations.literal: Shubao sent fifteen hundred carts loaded with rice to supply Shun and personally led five thousand picked troops to escort them.
translations.idiomatic: Shubao sent fifteen hundred carts loaded with rice to supply Shun and personally led five thousand picked troops as escort.

sentences.zh: 呂安國聞之，言於劉勉曰：「順精甲八千，而我眾不能居半。

translations.literal: When Lu Anguo heard of this, he said to Liu Mian: "Shun has eight thousand elite armor, and our numbers are not half his.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Anguo told Liu Mian: "Shun has eight thousand elite troops, and our numbers are less than half his.

sentences.zh: 相持既久，強弱勢殊，更復推遷，則無以自立。

translations.literal: We have been locked in stalemate so long that strong and weak are utterly unequal; if we delay further, we cannot stand.
translations.idiomatic: We have stalled so long that the odds have turned utterly against us; if we delay further, we cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 所賴者，彼糧行竭，我食有餘耳。

translations.literal: What we rely on is that their grain is exhausted while ours still holds;
translations.idiomatic: What we rely on is that their grain is gone while ours still holds;

sentences.zh: 若使叔寶米至，非唯難可復圖，我亦不能持久。

translations.literal: if Shubao's rice arrives, not only will victory be hard to win again—we cannot endure either.
translations.idiomatic: if Shubao's rice arrives, not only will victory be hard to win—we cannot endure either.

sentences.zh: 今唯有間道襲其米車，出彼不意，若能制之，當不戰走矣。」

translations.literal: Now we must take a hidden path and strike their grain carts by surprise; if we can seize them, they will flee without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: Now we must take a hidden path and strike their grain carts; if we seize them, they will flee without a fight."

sentences.zh: 勉以為然，以疲弱守營，簡精兵千人配安國及龍驤將軍黃回，使從間道出順後，於橫塘抄之。

translations.literal: Mian agreed, left the weak to hold the camp, picked a thousand elite troops and assigned them to Anguo and Dragon-Coursing general Huang Hui, and sent them by a hidden route behind Shun to raid at Hengtang.
translations.idiomatic: Mian agreed, left the weak to hold camp, picked a thousand elite troops for Anguo and Dragon-Coursing general Huang Hui, and sent them by a hidden route behind Shun to raid at Hengtang.

sentences.zh: 安國始行，繼二日熟食；

translations.literal: When Anguo set out, he had cooked food for two days;
translations.idiomatic: Anguo set out with cooked food for two days;

sentences.zh: 食盡，叔寶不至，將士欲還，安國曰：「卿等旦已一食。

translations.literal: the food was gone and Shubao had not come; the soldiers wished to return; Anguo said: "You have already eaten once today.
translations.idiomatic: the food ran out and Shubao had not come; the soldiers wished to return; Anguo said: "You have already eaten once today.

sentences.zh: 今晚米車不容不至；

translations.literal: Tonight the grain carts cannot fail to arrive;
translations.idiomatic: Tonight the grain carts cannot fail to arrive;

sentences.zh: 若其不至，夜去不晚。」

translations.literal: if they do not, it will not be too late to leave at night."
translations.idiomatic: if they do not, it will not be too late to leave at night."

sentences.zh: 叔寶果至，以米車為函箱陳，叔寶於外為遊軍。

translations.literal: Shubao indeed came, arraying the grain carts in box formation with Shubao himself as a mobile guard outside.
translations.idiomatic: Shubao came as expected, arraying the grain carts in box formation with himself as mobile guard outside.

sentences.zh: 幢主楊促懷將五百人居前，安國、回等擊斬之，及其士卒皆盡。

translations.literal: Standard-bearer Yang Cuihuai led five hundred men in the van; Anguo, Hui, and the others attacked, beheaded him, and destroyed all his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Standard-bearer Yang Cuihuai led five hundred men in the van; Anguo and Hui attacked, beheaded him, and destroyed all his men.

sentences.zh: 叔寶至，回欲乘勝擊之，安國曰：「彼將自走，不假復擊。」

translations.literal: When Shubao arrived, Hui wished to press the victory and attack; Anguo said: "He will flee of himself—no need to strike again."
translations.idiomatic: When Shubao arrived, Hui wished to press the attack; Anguo said: "He will flee of himself—no need to strike again."

sentences.zh: 退三十里，止宿。

translations.literal: They withdrew thirty li and encamped.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew thirty li and encamped.

sentences.zh: 夜遣騎參候，叔寶果棄米車走。

translations.literal: At night they sent horsemen to scout; Shubao indeed abandoned the grain carts and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At night they sent scouts; Shubao had abandoned the grain carts and fled.

sentences.zh: 安國復夜往燒米車，驅牛二千餘頭而還。

translations.literal: Anguo went again by night to burn the grain carts and drove back more than two thousand oxen.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo returned by night to burn the grain carts and drove back more than two thousand oxen.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁亥朔，夜，劉順眾潰，順走淮西就常珍奇。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on dinghai, the new moon, at night, Shun's force collapsed; Shun fled to Huaixi and joined Chang Zhenqi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dinghai, the new moon, at night, Shun's army collapsed; Shun fled to Huaixi and joined Chang Zhenqi.

sentences.zh: 於是劉勉鼓行，進向壽陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liu Mian beat the drums and advanced on Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Liu Mian beat the drums and advanced on Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 叔寶斂居民及散卒，嬰城自守；

translations.literal: Shubao gathered the inhabitants and scattered soldiers, drew up the city walls, and defended himself;
translations.idiomatic: Shubao gathered the townspeople and scattered troops, sealed the city, and held it in defense;

sentences.zh: 勉與諸軍分營城外。

translations.literal: Mian together with the various armies divided camps outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian and the other armies encamped outside the city in separate divisions.

sentences.zh: 山陽王休祐與殷琰書，為陳利害，上又遣御史王道隆繼詔宥琰罪。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shanyang, Liu Xiuyou, sent Yin Yan a letter setting forth gain and harm; the emperor also sent Censor Wang Daolong with successive edicts pardoning Yan's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shanyang Liu Xiuyou wrote to Yin Yan laying out the stakes, and the emperor also dispatched Censor Wang Daolong with repeated edicts forgiving Yan's offenses.

sentences.zh: 勉與琰書，並以琰兄瑗子邈書與之。

translations.literal: Mian also wrote to Yan and together sent Yan's elder brother Yuan's son Yao's letter to him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian wrote to Yin Yan as well and sent along a letter from Yan's nephew Yao, son of his brother Yuan.

sentences.zh: 琰與叔寶等皆有降意，而眾心不壹，復嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Yan and Shubao and the others all had intentions to surrender, but the hearts of the masses were not one, so again they drew up the city and held fast in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yan, Shubao, and the rest were all willing to submit, but the troops were divided in mind, and they again walled themselves in and defended stubbornly.

sentences.zh: 弋陽西山蠻田益之起兵應建康，詔以益之為輔國將軍。

translations.literal: The Yiyang western-hills barbarian Tian Yizhi raised troops in response to Jiankang; an edict appointed Yizhi General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yizhi of the western-hills barbarians in Yiyang rose in arms for Jiankang, and the court appointed him General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 督弋陽西山事。

translations.literal: Overseer of Yiyang western-hills affairs.
translations.idiomatic: With charge over affairs in the western hills of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以輔國將軍沈攸之為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On renchen, Auxiliary State General Shen Youzhi was appointed Yongzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, General Who Assists the State Shen Youzhi was appointed inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁未，以尚書左僕射王景文為中軍將軍。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Jingwen was made Central Army General.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Jingwen was appointed general of the central army.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以寧朔將軍劉乘民為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Pacifying the North General Liu Chengmin was made Jizhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, General Who Pacifies the North Liu Chengmin was appointed inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，葬昭太后修寧陵。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Empress Dowager Zhao was buried at Xiuning Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Empress Dowager Zhao was interred at Xiuning Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 張永、蕭道成等與薛索兒戰，大破之，索兒退保石樑；

translations.literal: Zhang Yong, Xiao Daocheng, and others fought Xue Suo'er and greatly defeated him; Suo'er withdrew to defend Shiliang;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong, Xiao Daocheng, and others fought Xue Suo'er and routed him; Suo'er fell back to defend Shiliang;

sentences.zh: 食盡而潰，走向樂平，為申令孫子孝叔所斬。

translations.literal: His provisions exhausted, his forces scattered; fleeing toward Leping, he was beheaded by Shen Lingsun's grandson Xiao Shuxiao.
translations.idiomatic: When his food ran out his men broke apart; fleeing toward Leping, he was beheaded by Shen Lingsun's grandson Xiao Shuxiao.

sentences.zh: 薛安都子道智走向合肥，詣裴季之降。

translations.literal: Xue Andu's son Daozhi fled toward Hefei and went to Pei Ji to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andu's son Daozhi fled to Hefei and submitted to Pei Ji.

sentences.zh: 傅靈越走至淮西，武衛將軍沛郡王廣之生獲之，送詣勉。

translations.literal: Fu Lingyue fled west of the Huai; Martial Guard General Prince of Peijun Wang Guangzhi captured him alive and sent him to Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lingyue fled to the Huai west; Martial Guard General Prince of Peijun Wang Guangzhi took him alive and sent him to Liu Mian.

sentences.zh: 勉詰其叛逆，靈越曰：「九州唱義，豈獨在我！

translations.literal: Mian interrogated him for rebellion; Lingyue said: "The Nine Provinces rose in righteous cause—how could the blame rest on me alone!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian questioned him about his rebellion; Lingyue said, "The Nine Provinces rose in righteous cause—why should I alone bear the guilt!

sentences.zh: 薛公不能專任智勇，委付子侄，此其所以敗也。

translations.literal: Lord Xue could not entrust wisdom and courage to one man alone but delegated to sons and nephews—this is why he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Xue could not keep command of wisdom and courage in his own hands but handed authority to sons and nephews—that is why he was beaten.

sentences.zh: 人生歸於一死，實無面求活。」

translations.literal: Human life returns to a single death; I truly have no face with which to beg for life."
translations.idiomatic: A man's life ends in death once; I truly have no face left with which to plead for my life."

sentences.zh: 送詣建康。

translations.literal: He was sent to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 上欲赦之，靈越辭終不改，乃殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to pardon him, but Lingyue's words never changed, so he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to spare him, but Lingyue's words never changed, and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 鄧琬以劉胡與沈攸之等相持，久不決，乃加袁顗督征討諸軍事。

translations.literal: Deng Wan, because Liu Hu and Shen Youzhi and others were locked in stalemate for long without decision, added Yuan Yi as supervisor of punitive campaign military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Because Liu Hu and Shen Youzhi remained deadlocked for so long, Deng Wan gave Yuan Yi overall command of the punitive armies.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲戌，顗帥樓船千艘，戰士二萬，來入鵲尾。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jiaxu, Yi led a thousand tower ships and twenty thousand fighting men and entered Quewei.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiaxu, Yuan Yi led a thousand tower ships and twenty thousand warriors into Quewei.

sentences.zh: 顗本無將略，性又怯橈，在軍中未嘗戎服，語不及戰陳，唯賦詩談義而已，不復撫接諸將；

translations.literal: Yi originally had no military strategy; his nature was also timid and yielding; in the army he never wore military dress, his talk never touched battle formations—only composing poetry and discussing principle; he no longer comforted and received the generals;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi had no gift for command and a timid, pliant nature; in camp he never wore armor, never spoke of battle arrays, only composed poetry and discoursed on doctrine, and no longer won over his generals;

sentences.zh: 劉胡每論事，酬對甚簡。

translations.literal: Whenever Liu Hu discussed affairs, the replies were very brief.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Liu Hu raised a matter, Yuan Yi's answers were terse.

sentences.zh: 由此大失人情，胡常切齒恚恨。

translations.literal: Because of this he greatly lost men's hearts; Hu constantly gnashed his teeth in furious resentment.
translations.idiomatic: By this he lost the goodwill of the army utterly; Hu gnashed his teeth in constant fury.

sentences.zh: 胡以南運米未至，軍士匱乏，就顗借襄陽之資，顗不許，曰：「都下兩宅未成，方應經理。」

translations.literal: Because southern transport grain had not arrived and the soldiers were depleted, Hu asked Yi to borrow Xiangyang resources; Yi refused, saying: "My two mansions in the capital are not yet finished—I must still manage them."
translations.idiomatic: Southern grain had not arrived and the troops were starving; Liu Hu asked Yuan Yi to lend him the resources of Xiangyang, but Yi refused, saying, "My two houses in the capital are unfinished—I still have to look after them."

sentences.zh: 又信往來之言，云「建康米貴，斗至數百」，以為將不攻自潰，擁甲以待之。

translations.literal: He also believed circulating reports saying "Grain in Jiankang is costly—a dou costs several hundred," thinking they would collapse without attack; he hugged his armor and waited.
translations.idiomatic: “He also believed travelers' reports that grain in Jiankang had soared to hundreds per dou, and expected the enemy to collapse without a fight—so he hugged his armor and waited.”

sentences.zh: 田益之帥蠻眾萬餘人圍義陽，鄧琬使司州刺史龐孟虯帥精兵五千救之，益之不戰潰去。

translations.literal: Tian Yizhi led more than ten thousand barbarian followers to besiege Yiyang; Deng Wan sent Sizhou inspector Pang Mengjiao with five thousand elite troops to rescue it; Yizhi fled without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yizhi led more than ten thousand barbarian warriors to besiege Yiyang; Deng Wan sent Sizhou inspector Pang Mengjiao with five thousand elite troops to relieve the city, and Yizhi broke camp and fled without fighting.

sentences.zh: 安成太守劉襲，始安內史王識之，建安內史趙道生，並舉郡來降。

translations.literal: Ancheng prefect Liu Xi, Shian interior minister Wang Shizhi, and Jian'an interior minister Zhao Daosheng all raised their commanderies and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Ancheng prefect Liu Xi, Shian interior minister Wang Shizhi, and Jian'an interior minister Zhao Daosheng all raised their commanderies and submitted.

sentences.zh: 襲，道憐之孫也。

translations.literal: Xi was the grandson of Liu Daolian.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was a grandson of Liu Daolian.

sentences.zh: 蕭道成世子賾為南康贛令，鄧琬遣使收系之。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng's heir Ze was magistrate of Gan in Nankang; Deng Wan sent messengers to seize and imprison him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng's heir Ze was magistrate of Gan in Nankang when Deng Wan sent men to seize and imprison him.

sentences.zh: 門客蘭陵桓康擔賾妻裴氏及其子長懋、子良逃於山中，與賾族人蕭欣祖等結客得百餘人，攻郡，破獄出賾。

translations.literal: Retainer Huan Kang of Lanling carried Ze's wife Lady Pei and sons Changmao and Ziliang into the mountains to escape; with Ze's clansman Xiao Xizu and others they gathered more than a hundred armed followers, attacked the commandery, broke the prison, and freed Ze.
translations.idiomatic: His retainer Huan Kang of Lanling carried off Ze's wife Lady Pei and sons Changmao and Ziliang into the hills; with Ze's kinsman Xiao Xizu and others they mustered more than a hundred fighting men, stormed the commandery, broke the jail, and freed Ze.

sentences.zh: 南康相沈肅之帥將吏追賾，賾與戰，擒之。

translations.literal: Nankang aide Shen Suzhi led officers and clerks in pursuit of Ze; Ze fought and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Nankang aide Shen Suzhi led officers and clerks in pursuit; Ze gave battle and took him captive.

sentences.zh: 賾自號寧朔將軍，據郡起兵，與劉襲等相應。

translations.literal: Ze styled himself General Who Pacifies the North, held the commandery and raised troops, coordinating with Liu Xi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Ze styled himself General Who Pacifies the North, seized the commandery and raised troops, and coordinated with Liu Xi and the others.

sentences.zh: 琬以中護軍殷孚為豫章太守，督上流五郡以防襲等。

translations.literal: Wan appointed Central Guardian Army Yin Fu prefect of Yuzhang to oversee the five upper-stream commanderies against Xi and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan appointed Central Guardian Army Yin Fu prefect of Yuzhang to oversee the five upper-stream commanderies against Liu Xi and his allies.

sentences.zh: 衡陽內史王應之起兵應建康，襲擊湘州行事何慧文於長沙。

translations.literal: Hengyang interior minister Wang Yingzhi raised troops in response to Jiankang and struck Xiangzhou acting inspector He Huiwen at Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Hengyang interior minister Wang Yingzhi rose for Jiankang and attacked Xiangzhou acting inspector He Huiwen at Changsha.

sentences.zh: 應之與慧文捨軍身戰，斫慧文八創，慧文斫應之斷足。

translations.literal: Yingzhi and Huiwen left their armies and fought in person; he hacked Huiwen with eight wounds; Huiwen hacked Yingzhi and severed his foot.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhi and Huiwen left their troops and fought hand to hand; Yingzhi cut Huiwen eight times, and Huiwen cut off Yingzhi's foot.

sentences.zh: 殺之。

translations.literal: He killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He killed him.

sentences.zh: 始興人劉嗣祖等據郡起兵應建康，廣州刺史袁曇遠遣其將李萬周等討之。

translations.literal: Liu Sizu of Shixing and others held the commandery and raised troops in response to Jiankang; Guangzhou inspector Yuan Tanyuan sent his generals Li Wanzhou and others to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sizu of Shixing and others seized the commandery and rose for Jiankang; Guangzhou inspector Yuan Tanyuan sent his generals Li Wanzhou and others against them.

sentences.zh: 嗣祖誑萬周云「尋陽已平」。

translations.literal: Sizu deceived Wanzhou, saying "Xunyang has already been pacified."
translations.idiomatic: Sizu deceived Wanzhou, saying, "Xunyang has already been pacified."

sentences.zh: 萬周還襲番禺，擒曇遠，斬之。

translations.literal: Wanzhou turned back, struck at Panyu, seized Tanyuan, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzhou turned back, struck Panyu, seized Tanyuan, and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 上以萬周行廣州事。

translations.literal: The emperor put Wanzhou in charge of Guangzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor put Li Wanzhou in charge of Guangzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，武都王楊元和治白水，微弱不能自立，棄國奔魏。

translations.literal: Earlier, King of Wudu Yang Yuanhe ruled Baishui; weak and unable to stand alone, he abandoned his state and fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, King of Wudu Yang Yuanhe had ruled at Baishui; too weak to stand alone, he abandoned his realm and fled to Wei.

sentences.zh: 元和從弟僧嗣復自立，屯葭蘆。

translations.literal: Yuanhe's younger cousin Sengsi restored independence and encamped at Jialu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhe's younger cousin Sengsi re-established his rule and encamped at Jialu.

sentences.zh: 費欣壽至巴東，巴東人任叔兒據白帝，自號輔國將軍，擊欣壽，斬之，叔兒遂阻守三峽。

translations.literal: Fei Xinshou reached Badong; Badong man Ren Shuer held Baidi, styled himself General Who Assists the State, attacked Xinshou and beheaded him; Shuer then blocked and held the Three Gorges.
translations.idiomatic: When Fei Xinshou reached Badong, the Badong native Ren Shuer seized Baidi, styled himself General Who Assists the State, attacked Xinshou and killed him, and then held the Three Gorges in blockade.

sentences.zh: 蕭惠開復遣治中程法度將兵三千出梁州，楊僧嗣帥群氐斷其道，間使以聞。

translations.literal: Xiao Huikai again sent Administrator of the Household Cheng Fadu with three thousand troops out from Liangzhou; Yang Sengsi led the Di tribes to cut his road and sent messengers between to report.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Huikai again sent household administrator Cheng Fadu with three thousand men out of Liangzhou; Yang Sengsi led the Di clans to cut his route and sent word through intermediaries.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁酉，以僧嗣為北秦州刺史、武都王。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingyou, Sengsi was appointed North Qinzhou inspector and King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingyou, Sengsi was appointed inspector of North Qinzhou and King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 諸軍與袁顗相拒於濃湖，久未決。

translations.literal: The various armies confronted Yuan Yi at Nonghu for a long time without decision.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial armies and Yuan Yi faced each other at Nonghu for a long time without a decision.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍張興世建議曰：「賊據上流，兵強地勝。

translations.literal: Dragon Cavalry General Zhang Xingshi proposed: "The rebels hold the upper stream—troops strong and terrain advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon Cavalry General Zhang Xingshi proposed, "The rebels hold the upper stream—strong in troops and favored by the ground.

sentences.zh: 我雖持之有餘，而制之不足。

translations.literal: Although we can hold our own with surplus, we lack enough to control them.
translations.idiomatic: We can hold our own, but we lack the means to master them.

sentences.zh: 若以奇兵數千潛出其上，因險而壁，見利而動，使其首尾周遑，進退疑阻，中流既梗，糧運自艱，此制賊之奇也。

translations.literal: If we send several thousand troops in a surprise move to slip out above them, fortify along the dangerous points, strike when there is advantage, make them waver head and tail, hesitate in advance and retreat—once the midstream is blocked, grain transport itself grows hard—this is the extraordinary means to control the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Send a few thousand picked men in secret above them, entrench on the defiles, strike when profit offers itself, throw them into confusion front and rear and doubt in advance and retreat—block the midstream and their grain route itself grows desperate. That is the extraordinary way to master the enemy.

sentences.zh: 錢溪江岸最狹，去大軍不遠，下臨洄洑，船下必來泊岸，又有橫浦可以藏船，千人守險，萬人不能過。

translations.literal: The Qianxi riverbank is narrowest, not far from the main army; below it overlooks the swirling eddies—boats descending must moor at the shore; there is also Hengpu where boats can hide; a thousand men guarding the danger, ten thousand cannot pass.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianxi bank is the narrowest stretch, close to our main force; below lie the swirling shallows where downstream boats must moor, and Hengpu can hide vessels—a thousand men on the defile and ten thousand cannot pass.

sentences.zh: 衝要之地，莫出於此。」

translations.literal: No choke point surpasses this."
translations.idiomatic: No strategic choke point surpasses this one."

sentences.zh: 沈攸之、吳喜並贊其策。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi and Wu Xi both praised his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi and Wu Xi both endorsed his plan.

sentences.zh: 會龐孟虯引兵來助殷琰，劉勉遣使求援甚急，建安王休仁欲遣興世救之。

translations.literal: Just then Pang Mengjiao led troops to aid Yin Yan; Liu Mian sent envoys urgently seeking relief; Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren wished to dispatch Xingshi to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Pang Mengjiao marched to aid Yin Yan; Liu Mian's appeals for help grew desperate, and Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren meant to send Xingshi to his relief.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之曰：「孟虯蟻聚，必無能為，遣別將馬步數千，足以相制。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi said: "Mengjiao is an ant swarm—they surely can do nothing; send a separate commander with several thousand horse and foot—that is enough to check them.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi said, "Mengjiao is only an ant swarm and can do nothing; send another commander with a few thousand horse and foot—that is enough to contain him.

sentences.zh: 興世之行，是安危大機。

translations.literal: Xingshi's mission is the great hinge of safety and peril.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi's mission is the great hinge of safety and peril.

sentences.zh: 必不可輟。」

translations.literal: It absolutely must not be halted."
translations.idiomatic: It must on no account be called off."

sentences.zh: 乃遣段佛榮將兵救勉，而選戰士七千、輕舸二百配興世。

translations.literal: So Duan Furong was sent with troops to relieve Mian, while seven thousand warriors and two hundred light boats were selected and assigned to Xingshi.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Duan Furong with troops to relieve Liu Mian and detached seven thousand picked warriors and two hundred light boats to Xingshi.

sentences.zh: 興世帥其眾溯流稍上，尋復退歸，如是者累日。

translations.literal: Xingshi led his men upstream a little, then soon withdrew again—this went on for days.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi led his force a little upstream, then withdrew again, and did so day after day.

sentences.zh: 劉胡聞之，笑曰：「我尚不敢越彼下取揚州，張興世何物人，欲輕據我上！」

translations.literal: Liu Hu heard and laughed: "I still dare not cross below them to take Yangzhou—what sort of man is Zhang Xingshi to want lightly to seize ground above me!"
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Hu heard this he laughed and said, "I myself do not yet dare slip past them downstream to take Yangzhou—what sort of nobody is Zhang Xingshi to think he can lightly seize ground above me!"

sentences.zh: 不為之備。

translations.literal: He made no preparation for it.
translations.idiomatic: He made no preparations against it.

sentences.zh: 一夕，四更，值便風，興世舉帆直前，渡湖、白，過鵲尾。

translations.literal: One night at the fourth watch, with a favorable wind, Xingshi raised sail and drove straight ahead, crossed Hubai, and passed Quewei.
translations.idiomatic: One night at the fourth watch, with a fair wind, Xingshi set sail straight ahead, crossed Hubai, and passed Quewei.

sentences.zh: 胡既覺，乃遣其將胡靈秀將兵於東岸翼之而進。

translations.literal: When Hu realized it, he sent his general Hu Lingxiu with troops on the eastern bank to flank and advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu discovered it, he sent his general Hu Lingxiu with troops along the eastern bank to flank him.

sentences.zh: 戊戌夕，興世宿景洪浦，靈秀亦留。

translations.literal: On the evening of wuxu, Xingshi encamped at Jinghong Ford; Lingxiu also halted.
translations.idiomatic: On the evening of wuxu, Xingshi lay at Jinghong Ford, and Lingxiu halted as well.

sentences.zh: 興世潛遣其將黃道標帥七十舸徑趣錢溪，立營寨；

translations.literal: Xingshi secretly sent his general Huang Daobiao with seventy boats directly for Qianxi to establish a stockade;
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi secretly sent his general Huang Daobiao with seventy boats straight for Qianxi to raise a stockade;

sentences.zh: 己亥，興世引兵進據之，靈秀不能禁。

translations.literal: On jihai, Xingshi led troops forward to occupy it; Lingxiu could not stop him.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Xingshi advanced and seized the position; Lingxiu could not prevent him.

sentences.zh: 庚子，劉胡自將水步二十六軍來攻錢溪。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Liu Hu personally led twenty-six armies of water and foot to attack Qianxi.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Liu Hu personally led twenty-six combined water and land armies against Qianxi.

sentences.zh: 將士欲迎擊據之，興世禁之曰：「賊來尚遠，氣盛而矢驟；

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers wished to meet the attack and seize the position; Xingshi forbade them, saying: "The rebels are still far off—morale is high and arrows will come fast;
translations.idiomatic: His officers wanted to meet the attack at once; Xingshi forbade them, saying, "The enemy is still far off—his spirit is high and his arrows will fly thick;

sentences.zh: 驟既易盡，盛亦易衰，不如待之。」

translations.literal: what comes fast is easily spent, what is high is easily spent down—better to wait."
translations.idiomatic: what comes fast is soon spent, what burns high soon fades—better to wait."

sentences.zh: 令將士治城如故。

translations.literal: He ordered the soldiers to fortify the rampart as before.
translations.idiomatic: He had his men go on fortifying the rampart as before.

sentences.zh: 俄而胡來轉近，船入洄洑；

translations.literal: Soon Hu came closer and closer; boats entered the swirling current;
translations.idiomatic: Before long Hu drew nearer and his boats entered the swirling shallows;

sentences.zh: 興世命壽寂之、任農夫帥壯士數百擊之，眾軍相繼並進，胡敗走，斬首數百，胡收兵而下。

translations.literal: Xingshi ordered Shou Jizhi and Ren Nongfu to lead several hundred stalwarts to strike; the armies followed in succession; Hu was defeated and fled, several hundred heads were taken, and Hu withdrew his troops downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi ordered Shou Jizhi and Ren Nongfu to lead several hundred stalwarts in the attack; the main force followed in waves; Hu was beaten and fled, several hundred heads were taken, and Hu drew his troops downstream.

sentences.zh: 時興世城寨未固，建安王休仁慮袁覬並力更攻錢溪，欲分其勢。

translations.literal: At that time Xingshi's stockade was not yet firm; Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren feared Yuan Yi would combine forces to attack Qianxi again and wished to divide his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi's stockade was not yet secure; Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren feared Yuan Yi would mass his strength for another assault on Qianxi and wished to divide the enemy.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，命沈攸之、吳喜等以皮艦進攻濃湖，斬獲千數。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Shen Youzhi, Wu Xi, and others were ordered to attack Nonghu with leather warships, beheading and capturing thousands.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, he ordered Shen Youzhi, Wu Xi, and others to attack Nonghu with leather warships, taking a thousand heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 是日，劉胡帥步卒二萬、鐵馬一千，欲更攻興世。

translations.literal: That day Liu Hu led twenty thousand foot soldiers and a thousand armored horses, intending again to attack Xingshi.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Liu Hu led twenty thousand foot soldiers and a thousand armored horsemen to strike Xingshi again.

sentences.zh: 未至錢溪數十里，袁覬以濃湖之急，遽追之，錢溪城由此得立。

translations.literal: Before reaching Qianxi by several tens of li, Yuan Yi, because of the crisis at Nonghu, hurriedly recalled him, and the Qianxi fortress was thereby secured.
translations.idiomatic: When he was still several tens of li from Qianxi, Yuan Yi, pressed by the crisis at Nonghu, recalled him in haste, and the Qianxi fortress was thereby saved.

sentences.zh: 胡遣人傳唱「錢溪已平」，眾並懼，沈攸之曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Hu sent men to spread the cry "Qianxi has been pacified"; everyone was afraid; Shen Youzhi said: "That is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Hu had men spread the cry that Qianxi had fallen; the army was alarmed; Shen Youzhi said, "That is not so.

sentences.zh: 若錢溪實敗，萬人中應有一人逃亡得還者；

translations.literal: If Qianxi had truly fallen, among ten thousand men at least one fugitive should have returned;
translations.idiomatic: If Qianxi had truly been lost, of ten thousand men at least one fugitive should have made it back;

sentences.zh: 必是彼戰失利，唱空聲以惑眾耳。」

translations.literal: they must have lost the battle and are raising empty cries to confuse the masses."
translations.idiomatic: they must have lost the fight and are shouting empty boasts to confuse our ranks."

sentences.zh: 勒軍中不得妄動；

translations.literal: He ordered the army not to stir rashly;
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the army not to stir rashly;

sentences.zh: 錢溪捷報尋至。

translations.literal: news of Qianxi's victory soon arrived.
translations.idiomatic: News of victory at Qianxi soon arrived.

sentences.zh: 攸之以錢溪所送胡軍耳鼻示濃湖，袁覬駭懼。

translations.literal: Youzhi displayed to Nonghu the ears and noses of Hu's army sent from Qianxi; Yuan Yi was terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi displayed at Nonghu the ears and noses of Liu Hu's men sent from Qianxi, and Yuan Yi was stricken with fear.

sentences.zh: 攸之日幕引歸。

translations.literal: Youzhi withdrew at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi withdrew at dusk.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍劉道符攻山陽，程天祚請降。

translations.literal: Dragon Cavalry General Liu Daofu attacked Shanyang; Cheng Tianzuo requested to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon Cavalry General Liu Daofu attacked Shanyang, and Cheng Tianzuo offered to surrender.

sentences.zh: 龐孟虯進至弋陽，劉勉遣呂安國等迎擊於蓼潭，大破之，孟虯走向義陽。

translations.literal: Pang Mengjiao advanced to Yiyang; Liu Mian sent Lü Anguo and others to meet and strike him at Liaotan, routing him greatly; Mengjiao fled toward Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Mengjiao advanced to Yiyang; Liu Mian sent Lü Anguo and others to meet him at Liaotan and routed him; Mengjiao fled toward Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 王玄謨之子曇善起兵據義陽以應建康，孟虯走死蠻中。

translations.literal: Wang Xuemo's son Tanshan raised troops and held Yiyang in support of Jiankang; Mengjiao fled and died among the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuemo's son Tanshan rose and seized Yiyang for Jiankang; Mengjiao fled and died among the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 劉胡遣輔國將軍薛道標襲合肥，殺汝陰太守裴季，劉勉遣輔國將軍垣閎擊之。

translations.literal: Liu Hu sent Auxiliary State General Xue Daobiao to raid Hefei, killing Ruyin prefect Pei Ji; Liu Mian sent Auxiliary State General Yuan Hong to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu sent General Who Assists the State Xue Daobiao to raid Hefei and kill Ruyin prefect Pei Ji; Liu Mian sent General Who Assists the State Yuan Hong against him.

sentences.zh: 閎，閬之弟；

translations.literal: Hong was the younger brother of Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was a younger brother of Yuan Lang.

sentences.zh: 道標，安都之子也。

translations.literal: Daobiao was Andu's son.
translations.idiomatic: Daobiao was a son of Xue Andu.

sentences.zh: 淮西人鄭叔舉起兵擊常珍奇以應鄭黑；

translations.literal: Huai west man Zheng Shuju raised troops to attack Chang Zhenqi in coordination with Zheng Hei;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shuju of the Huai west rose in arms against Chang Zhenqi in concert with Zheng Hei;

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以叔舉為北豫州刺史。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Shuju was appointed North Yuzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Shuju was appointed inspector of North Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 崔道固為土人所攻，閉門自守。

translations.literal: Cui Daogu was attacked by local people and shut his gates to defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Daogu was beset by local forces and shut his gates to hold out.

sentences.zh: 上遣使宣慰，道固請降。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to reassure him; Daogu requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to reassure him, and Daogu asked to submit.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，復以道固為徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Daogu was again appointed Xuzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Daogu was again appointed inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 八月，皇甫道烈等聞龐孟虯，並開門出降。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Huangfu Daolie and others, upon hearing of Pang Mengjiao, all opened their gates and came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Huangfu Daolie and others, hearing of Pang Mengjiao's fall, all opened their gates and submitted.

sentences.zh: 張興世既據錢溪，濃湖軍乏食。

translations.literal: Zhang Xingshi having seized Qianxi, the Nonghu army lacked food.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhang Xingshi held Qianxi, the army at Nonghu ran short of food.

sentences.zh: 鄧琬大送資糧，畏興世，不敢進。

translations.literal: Deng Wan sent abundant supplies, but feared Xingshi and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan sent great stores of grain, but feared Xingshi and dared not push forward.

sentences.zh: 劉胡帥輕舸四百，由鵲頭內路欲攻錢溪，既而謂長史王念叔：「吾少習步戰，未閒水鬥。

translations.literal: Liu Hu led four hundred light boats by the inner route from Quetou intending to attack Qianxi; then he said to chief clerk Wang Nianshu: "I studied foot combat when young and am not practiced in water fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu led four hundred light boats along the inner route from Quetou to attack Qianxi, then said to his chief clerk Wang Nianshu, "I trained in infantry fighting when young and am unskilled in water combat.

sentences.zh: 若步戰，恆在數萬人中；

translations.literal: In foot combat I am always among tens of thousands of men;
translations.idiomatic: On land I am always among tens of thousands of men;

sentences.zh: 水戰在一舸之上，舸舸各進，不複相關，正在三十人中，此非萬全之計，吾不為也。」

translations.literal: In water combat one is upon a single boat; boat by boat each advances, no longer mutually linked—one is right among thirty men; this is not a plan of complete safety; I will not do it."
translations.idiomatic: In a river fight you stand on one boat while each vessel advances alone, cut off from the rest—you are one man among thirty. That is no sure plan; I will not attempt it."

sentences.zh: 乃托瘧疾，住鵲頭不進，遣龍驤將軍陳慶將三百舸向錢溪，戒慶：「不須戰。

translations.literal: He then pleaded malaria, halted at Quetou and did not advance, and sent Dragon Cavalry General Chen Qing leading three hundred boats toward Qianxi, admonishing Qing: "Do not fight.
translations.idiomatic: He then claimed malaria, held at Quetou without advancing, and sent Dragon Cavalry General Chen Qing with three hundred boats toward Qianxi, warning him, "Do not give battle.

sentences.zh: 張興世吾之所悉，自當走耳。」

translations.literal: Zhang Xingshi is one I know well; he will of himself flee."
translations.idiomatic: I know Zhang Xingshi well enough—he will retreat on his own."

sentences.zh: 陳慶至錢溪，軍於梅根。

translations.literal: Chen Qing reached Qianxi and encamped at Megan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qing reached Qianxi and made camp at Megan.

sentences.zh: 胡遣別將王起將百舸攻興世，興世擊起，大破之。

translations.literal: Hu sent deputy general Wang Qi leading a hundred boats to attack Xingshi; Xingshi struck Qi and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Hu sent his deputy Wang Qi with a hundred boats against Xingshi; Xingshi attacked Qi and smashed his force.

sentences.zh: 胡帥其餘舸馳還，謂顗曰：「興世營寨已立，不可猝攻；

translations.literal: Hu led the remaining boats galloping back and said to Yi: "Xingshi's fortified camp is already established; it cannot be rushed in attack;
translations.idiomatic: Hu raced back with the surviving boats and told Yuan Yi, "Xingshi has already built his camp—we cannot storm it in haste;

sentences.zh: 昨日小戰，未足為損。

translations.literal: yesterday's small fight is not sufficient to count as loss.
translations.idiomatic: yesterday's skirmish was no real harm.

sentences.zh: 陳慶已與南陵、大雷諸軍共遏其上，大軍在此，鵲頭諸將又斷其下流；

translations.literal: Chen Qing has already with the armies of Nanling and Dalei together blocked them above; the great army is here, and the generals at Quetou again cut off their lower stream;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qing has joined the Nanling and Dalei forces to pin them from above, our main body is here, and the generals at Quetou have cut their downstream route;

sentences.zh: 已墮圍中，不足復慮。」

translations.literal: they have already fallen into encirclement—not worth further worry."
translations.idiomatic: they are already trapped in a siege—there is nothing more to fear."

sentences.zh: 覬怒胡不戰，謂曰：「糧運鯁塞，當如此何？」

translations.literal: Yi was angry that Hu would not fight and said: "Grain transport is choked—what is to be done about this?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi raged at Hu for refusing battle and demanded, "Our grain route is blocked—what do we do now?"

sentences.zh: 胡曰：「彼尚得溯流越我而上，此運何以不得沿流越彼而下邪！」

translations.literal: Hu said: "They can still go upstream past us upward—why cannot this transport go downstream past them downward!"
translations.idiomatic: Hu replied, "If they can still fight upstream past us, why cannot our supply line run downstream past them?"

sentences.zh: 乃遣安北府司馬沈仲玉將千人步趣南陵迎糧。

translations.literal: He then sent Northern Pacification headquarters marshal Shen Zhongyu with a thousand men on foot toward Nanling to meet the grain.
translations.idiomatic: He then dispatched Northern Pacification headquarters marshal Shen Zhongyu with a thousand infantry toward Nanling to fetch the grain.

sentences.zh: 仲玉至南陵，載米三十萬斛，錢布數十舫，豎榜為城，規欲突過。

translations.literal: Zhongyu reached Nanling, loaded three hundred thousand hu of rice, and several tens of boats of coin and cloth, set up placards as a wall, and planned to burst through.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyu reached Nanling, loaded three hundred thousand hu of rice and dozens of boats carrying coin and cloth, raised placards to form a protective wall, and intended to force a passage through.

sentences.zh: 行至貴口，不敢進，遣間信報胡，令遣重軍援接。

translations.literal: On reaching Guikou he dared not advance, sent a secret messenger to report to Hu, and ordered him to send a heavy army to support and link up.
translations.idiomatic: At Guikou he halted, too afraid to press on, sent a secret courier to Hu asking for a strong relief force.

sentences.zh: 張興世遣壽寂之、任農夫等將三千人至貴口擊之，仲玉走還顗營，悉虜其資實；

translations.literal: Zhang Xingshi sent Shou Jizhi, Ren Nongfu, and others leading three thousand men to Guikou to strike them; Zhongyu fled back to Yi's camp, and all his supplies and goods were captured;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xingshi sent Shou Jizhi, Ren Nongfu, and others with three thousand men to strike at Guikou; Zhongyu fled back to Yuan Yi's camp and lost all his stores and wealth;

sentences.zh: 胡眾駭懼，胡將張喜來降。

translations.literal: Hu's troops were terrified; Hu's general Zhang Xi came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Hu's soldiers panicked, and his officer Zhang Xi defected.

sentences.zh: 鎮東中兵參軍劉亮進兵逼胡營，胡不能制。

translations.literal: Eastern Pacification central corps army adviser Liu Liang advanced troops to press Hu's camp; Hu could not control it.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Pacification central corps adviser Liu Liang pressed Hu's camp with his troops; Hu could not hold his ground.

sentences.zh: 袁顗懼曰：「賊入人肝脾裡，何由得活！」

translations.literal: Yuan Yi in fear said: "The bandits have entered men's liver and spleen—how can one live!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi said in terror, "The enemy is in our vitals—how can we survive!"

sentences.zh: 胡陰謀遁去，己卯，誑覬云：「欲更帥步騎二萬，上取錢溪，兼下大雷餘運。」

translations.literal: Hu secretly plotted to flee; on jimao he deceived Yi saying: "I wish again to lead twenty thousand foot and horse, go up to take Qianxi, and also bring down the remaining transport at Dalei."
translations.idiomatic: Hu secretly planned to escape; on jimao he lied to Yuan Yi, saying, "I wish to lead twenty thousand infantry and cavalry upstream to seize Qianxi and also escort Dalei's remaining supplies downstream."

sentences.zh: 令覬悉選馬配之。

translations.literal: He ordered Yi to select all horses and assign them to him.
translations.idiomatic: He had Yuan Yi gather every available mount for him.

sentences.zh: 其日，胡委覬去，逕趣梅根。

translations.literal: That day Hu abandoned Yi and left, going straight to Megan.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Hu abandoned Yuan Yi and fled straight for Megan.

sentences.zh: 先令薛常寶辦船，悉發南陵諸軍，燒大雷諸城而走。

translations.literal: He first ordered Xue Changbao to prepare boats, mustered all the Nanling armies, burned the cities of Dalei, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: First he had Xue Changbao ready the boats, called up all forces at Nanling, burned the towns of Dalei, and ran.

sentences.zh: 至夜，覬方知之，大怒，罵曰：「今年為小子所誤！」

translations.literal: By night Yi only then knew; he was greatly angry and cursed: "This year I was misled by that stripling!"
translations.idiomatic: Only at night did Yuan Yi learn of it. He raged and cursed, "This year that whelp has ruined me!"

sentences.zh: 呼取常所乘善馬「飛燕」謂其眾曰：「我當自出追之！」

translations.literal: He summoned his usual fine mount "Flying Swallow" and said to his troops: "I myself shall go out in pursuit!"
translations.idiomatic: He called for his favorite charger Flying Swallow and told his men, "I will pursue him myself!"

sentences.zh: 因亦走。

translations.literal: He then fled as well.
translations.idiomatic: And he fled too.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，建安王休仁勒兵入覬營，納降卒十萬，遣沈攸之等追顗。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Prince of Jian'an Xiuren led troops into Yi's camp, received one hundred thousand surrendering soldiers, and sent Shen Youzhi and others in pursuit of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren marched into Yuan Yi's camp, took the surrender of a hundred thousand men, and sent Shen Youzhi and others to hunt Yuan Yi.

sentences.zh: 顗走至鵲頭，與戍主薛伯珍並所領數千人偕去，欲向尋陽。

translations.literal: Yi fled to Quetou, and with garrison commander Xue Bozhen and the several thousand he led went off together, intending toward Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi fled to Quetou; with garrison commander Xue Bozhen and a few thousand followers he set out for Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 夜，止山間，殺馬以勞將士，顧謂伯珍曰：「我非不能死；

translations.literal: At night they halted in the mountains, killed horses to refresh the officers and soldiers, and Yi turning to Bozhen said: "It is not that I cannot die;
translations.idiomatic: At night they stopped in the hills, slaughtered horses to refresh the troops, and Yuan Yi turned to Bozhen and said, "It is not that I lack the courage to die;

sentences.zh: 且欲一至尋陽，謝罪主上，然後自刎耳。」

translations.literal: I only wish first to reach Xunyang, confess fault to the sovereign, and then cut my own throat."
translations.idiomatic: I only want to reach Xunyang once, apologize to the throne, and then take my own life."

sentences.zh: 因慷慨叱左右索節，無復應者。

translations.literal: He then in high spirit shouted at attendants to seek his tally—there was none who answered.
translations.idiomatic: He cried out for his tally of command, but no one responded.

sentences.zh: 及旦，伯珍請屏人言事，遂斬顗首，詣錢溪馬軍主襄陽俞湛之。

translations.literal: When dawn came Bozhen asked to dismiss the crowd to speak of affairs and then cut off Yi's head, and went to Qianxi cavalry commander Yu Zhanzhi of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Bozhen asked for a private word, then struck off Yuan Yi's head and went to Yu Zhanzhi, cavalry commander at Qianxi from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 湛之因斬伯珍，並送首以為己功。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi then cut off Bozhen and sent both heads as his own achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi killed Bozhen as well and forwarded both heads as his own exploit.

sentences.zh: 劉胡帥二萬人向尋陽，詐晉安王子勳云：「袁覬已降，軍皆散，唯己帥所領獨返；

translations.literal: Liu Hu led twenty thousand men toward Xunyang and falsely told the Prince of Jin'an Zixun: "Yuan Yi has already surrendered, the armies have all dispersed—only the force I lead has returned alone;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu led twenty thousand men toward Xunyang and lied to Prince of Jin'an Liu Zixun, "Yuan Yi has surrendered, the armies have broken up—only my contingent has returned;

sentences.zh: 宜速處分，為一戰之資。

translations.literal: you should quickly dispose affairs and make means for one battle.
translations.idiomatic: act at once and ready what you need for one last fight.

sentences.zh: 當停據湓城，誓死不貳。」

translations.literal: We should halt and hold Pencheng, vowing death and no second loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: We must hold Pencheng and swear to die without wavering."

sentences.zh: 乃於江外夜趣沔口。

translations.literal: He then by night outside the river hurried to Miankou.
translations.idiomatic: Then he marched by night along the outer Yangtze toward Miankou.

sentences.zh: 鄧琬聞胡去，憂惶無計，呼中書舍人褚靈嗣等謀之，並不知所出。

translations.literal: Deng Wan hearing Hu had gone was anxious without plan, summoned Secretariat Gentlemen Chu Lingsi and others to deliberate, and none knew what course to take.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Wan heard Liu Hu had fled, panic left him no plan; he called Secretariat Gentlemen Chu Lingsi and others to counsel, and none could suggest a way out.

sentences.zh: 張悅詐稱疾，呼琬計事，令左右伏甲帳後，戒之：「若聞索酒，便出。」

translations.literal: Zhang Yue falsely claimed illness, summoned Wan to discuss affairs, ordered attendants to hide armor behind the tent, and warned them: "If you hear a request for wine, then come out."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue feigned illness, summoned Wan to discuss strategy, hid armed men behind the tent screen, and instructed them, "When you hear him call for wine, come out."

sentences.zh: 琬既至，悅曰：「卿首唱此謀，今事已急，計將安出！」

translations.literal: When Wan had arrived Yue said: "You first raised this plot—now matters are urgent—where will the plan come out!"
translations.idiomatic: When Wan arrived Zhang Yue said, "You launched this conspiracy—now we are cornered. What is your plan?"

sentences.zh: 琬曰：「正當斬晉安王，封府庫，以謝罪耳。」

translations.literal: Wan said: "We should rightly behead the Prince of Jin'an, seal the treasury storehouses, and thereby confess fault."
translations.idiomatic: Wan said, "We should behead the Prince of Jin'an, seal the treasury, and sue for mercy."

sentences.zh: 悅曰：「寧可賣殿下求活邪！」

translations.literal: Yue said: "How could one sell His Highness to seek life!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue cried, "Would you betray His Highness to save your own skin?"

sentences.zh: 因呼酒。

translations.literal: He then called for wine.
translations.idiomatic: He called for wine.

sentences.zh: 子洵提刀出，斬琬。

translations.literal: Zi Xun drew his blade and came out, beheading Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Xun stepped out with his blade and slew Wan.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人潘欣之聞琬死，勒兵而至。

translations.literal: Secretariat Gentleman Pan Xinzhi hearing Wan was dead mustered troops and arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Gentleman Pan Xinzhi, hearing Wan was dead, marched in with troops.

sentences.zh: 悅使人語之曰：「鄧琬謀反，今已梟戮。」

translations.literal: Yue had someone tell him: "Deng Wan plotted rebellion and has now been beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue sent word, "Deng Wan rebelled and has been executed."

sentences.zh: 欣之乃還。

translations.literal: Xinzhi then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Xinzhi withdrew.

sentences.zh: 取琬子，並殺之。

translations.literal: He took Wan's sons and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Wan's sons and killed them too.

sentences.zh: 悅因單舸繼琬首馳下，詣建安王休仁降。

translations.literal: Yue then in a single boat followed Wan's head galloping downstream, went to Prince of Jian'an Xiuren, and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue took a lone boat, Wan's head in tow, raced downstream, and surrendered to Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren.

sentences.zh: 尋陽亂。

translations.literal: Xunyang fell into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Xunyang erupted in chaos.

sentences.zh: 蔡那之子道淵在尋陽被系作部，脫鎖入城，執子勳，囚之。

translations.literal: Cai Na's son Daoyuan at Xunyang was bound as corvee labor; he broke his shackles, entered the city, seized Zixun, and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Na's son Daoyuan, conscripted as corvee labor at Xunyang, broke his chains, entered the city, seized Liu Zixun, and held him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之等諸軍至尋陽，斬晉安王子勳，傳首建康，時年十一。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi and the various armies reached Xunyang, beheaded the Prince of Jin'an Zixun, and sent the head to Jiankang; he was eleven sui.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi and the other armies reached Xunyang they beheaded Prince of Jin'an Liu Zixun and sent his head to Jiankang; he was eleven years old.

sentences.zh: 初，鄧琬遣臨川內史張淹自鄱陽嶠道入三吳，軍於上饒，聞劉胡敗，軍副鄱陽太守費曄斬淹以降。

translations.literal: Earlier Deng Wan had sent Administrator of Linchuan Zhang Yan from the Poyang pass route into the Three Wu, encamping at Shangrao; hearing Liu Hu was defeated, army deputy Administrator of Poyang Fei Ye beheaded Yan and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Deng Wan had sent Linchuan administrator Zhang Yan through the Poyang pass into the Three Wu, where he camped at Shangrao; when he heard of Liu Hu's defeat, his deputy Fei Ye, Poyang administrator, beheaded Yan and submitted.

sentences.zh: 淹，暢之子也。

translations.literal: Yan was the son of Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan was a son of Zhang Chang.

sentences.zh: 廢帝之世，衣冠懼禍，鹹欲遠出。

translations.literal: In the era of the Deposed Emperor, officials and gentry feared calamity and all wished to go far away.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Deposed Emperor, gentlemen of office feared ruin and all longed to flee afar.

sentences.zh: 至是流離外難，百不一存，眾乃服蔡興宗之先見。

translations.literal: By now displaced in outer calamity, not one in a hundred survived, and the multitude then submitted to Cai Xingzong's foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Now scattered by war abroad, scarcely one in a hundred survived, and men at last acknowledged Cai Xingzong's foresight.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬辰，以山陽王休祐為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on renchen, Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was made Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renchen, Prince of Shanyang Liu Xiuyou was appointed inspector of Jing.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，解嚴，大赦。

translations.literal: On guisi, the alert was lifted and a general amnesty proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the martial law was lifted and a great amnesty declared.

sentences.zh: 庚子，司徒休仁至尋陽，遣吳喜、張興世向荊州，沈懷明向郢州，劉亮及寧朔將軍南陽張敬兒向雍州，孫超之向湘州，沈思仁、任農夫向豫章，平定餘寇。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Minister over the Masses Xiuren reached Xunyang, sent Wu Xi and Zhang Xingshi toward Jing Province, Shen Huaiming toward Ying Province, Liu Liang and Pacifying-the-North General Zhang Jinger of Nanyang toward Yong Province, Sun Chaozhi toward Xiang Province, Shen Siren and Ren Nongfu toward Yuzhang, to pacify the remaining bandits.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Grand Minister Liu Xiuren reached Xunyang and dispatched Wu Xi and Zhang Xingshi to Jing, Shen Huaiming to Ying, Liu Liang and Pacifying-the-North general Zhang Jinger of Nanyang to Yong, Sun Chaozhi to Xiang, and Shen Siren and Ren Nongfu to Yuzhang to mop up the remaining rebels.

sentences.zh: 劉胡逃至石城，捕得，斬之。

translations.literal: Liu Hu fled to Shicheng, was captured, and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu fled to Shicheng, was taken, and executed.

sentences.zh: 郢州行事張沈變形為沙門，潛走，追獲，殺之。

translations.literal: Acting prefect of Ying Zhang Shen disguised his form as a monk, fled secretly, was pursued and captured, and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's acting prefect Zhang Shen shaved his head like a monk and slipped away, but was hunted down and killed.

sentences.zh: 荊州行事劉道憲聞濃湖平，散兵，遣使歸罪。

translations.literal: Acting prefect of Jing Liu Daoxian hearing Nonghu was pacified dispersed his troops and sent envoys to return in guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's acting prefect Liu Daoxian, learning Nonghu had fallen, disbanded his troops and sent envoys to surrender.

sentences.zh: 荊州治中宗景等勒兵入城，殺道憲，執臨海王子頊以降。

translations.literal: Jing Administrator-in-chief Zong Jing and others mustered troops into the city, killed Daoxian, seized the Prince of Linhai Zixu, and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Jing chief administrator Zong Jing and others marched into the city, killed Liu Daoxian, seized Prince of Linhai Liu Zixu, and submitted.

sentences.zh: 孔道存知尋陽已平，遣使請降；

translations.literal: Kong Daocun knowing Xunyang was already pacified sent envoys to request surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Kong Daocun, learning Xunyang had fallen, sent envoys to sue for peace;

sentences.zh: 尋聞柳世隆、劉亮當至，眾悉逃潰，道存及三子皆自殺。

translations.literal: soon hearing Liu Shilong and Liu Liang were about to arrive, the masses all fled in rout, and Daocun and his three sons all killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: but when word came that Liu Shilong and Liu Liang were approaching, his troops scattered; Daocun and his three sons all took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 上以何慧文才兼將吏，使吳喜宣旨赦之。

translations.literal: The emperor because He Huiwen's talent combined general and clerk, sent Wu Xi to proclaim the edict pardoning him.
translations.idiomatic: Because He Huiwen was skilled as both commander and administrator, the emperor sent Wu Xi to proclaim a pardon.

sentences.zh: 慧文曰：「既陷逆節，手害忠義，何面見天下之士！」

translations.literal: Huiwen said: "Having already fallen into rebellious conduct and personally harming the loyal and righteous—what face to meet the gentlemen of the realm!"
translations.idiomatic: He Huiwen replied, "I took the rebel path and killed loyal men with my own hands—what face have I to show the empire's officers?"

sentences.zh: 遂自殺。

translations.literal: He then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: He then killed himself.

sentences.zh: 安陸王子綏、臨海王子頊、邵陵王子無並賜死，劉順及餘黨在荊州者皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Prince of Anlu Zisui, Prince of Linhai Zixu, and Prince of Shaoling Ziwu were all granted death; Liu Shun and the remaining partisans in Jing Province were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Princes of Anlu, Linhai, and Shaoling were all ordered to die; Liu Shun and the rest of the rebel faction in Jing were put to death.

sentences.zh: 詔追贈諸死節之臣，及封賞有功者各有差。

translations.literal: An edict pursued posthumous ennoblement of the various ministers who died in loyalty, and enfeoffment and rewards for the meritorious each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered posthumous honors for those who died loyal and graded rewards for the victorious.

sentences.zh: 己酉，魏初立郡學，置博士、助教、生員，從中書令高允、相州刺史李言斤之請也。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Wei first established commandery schools, setting Erudites, assistant instructors, and student members, following the request of Secretariat Director Gao Yun and Regional Inspector of Xiangzhou Li Yanjin.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Northern Wei established commandery schools with Erudites, assistants, and enrolled students, at the request of Secretariat Director Gao Yun and Xiangzhou inspector Li Yanjin.

sentences.zh: 言斤，崇之子也。

translations.literal: Yanjin was the son of Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanjin was a son of Li Chong.

sentences.zh: 上既誅晉安王子勳等，待世祖諸子猶如平日。

translations.literal: The emperor having already executed the Prince of Jin'an Zixun and others, still treated the Former Emperor's sons as on ordinary days.
translations.idiomatic: After executing Prince of Jin'an Liu Zixun and the others, the emperor still treated the late emperor's sons as before.

sentences.zh: 司徒休仁還自尋陽，言於上曰：「松滋侯兄弟尚在，將來非社稷計，宜早為之所。」

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Xiuren returned from Xunyang and said to the emperor: "The Marquis of Songzi's brothers still survive—in the future this is not a plan for the altars of soil and grain; we should early take measures regarding them."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister Liu Xiuren returned from Xunyang and told the emperor, "The Marquis of Songzi's brothers still live—that will not serve the throne's future. Deal with them soon."

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙卯，松滋侯子房、永嘉王子仁、始安王子真、淮南王子孟、南平王子產、廬陵王子輿、子趨、子期、東平王子嗣、子悅並賜死，及鎮北咨議參軍路休之、司徒從事中郎路茂之、兗州刺史劉祗、中書舍人嚴龍皆坐誅。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on yimao, Marquis of Songzi Zifang, Prince of Yongjia Ziren, Prince of Shi'an Zizhen, Prince of Huainan Zimeng, Prince of Nanping Zichan, Prince of Luling Ziyu, Ziqu, Ziqi, Prince of Dongping Zisi, and Ziyue were all granted death, and Northern Pacification adviser Lu Xiuzhi, Secretariat attendant Lu Maozhi, Inspector of Yanzhou Liu Zhi, and Secretariat Gentleman Yan Long were all implicated and executed.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on yimao, Marquis of Songzi Liu Zifang, Princes of Yongjia, Shi'an, Huainan, Nanping, and Luling, Liu Ziqu, Liu Ziqi, Prince of Dongping Liu Zisi, and Liu Ziyue were all ordered to die, along with Northern Pacification adviser Lu Xiuzhi, secretariat attendant Lu Maozhi, Yanzhou inspector Liu Zhi, and secretariat gentleman Yan Long.

sentences.zh: 世祖二十八子於此盡矣。

translations.literal: The Former Emperor's twenty-eight sons were at this point all gone.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's twenty-eight sons were extinguished here.

sentences.zh: 祗，義欣之子也。

translations.literal: Zhi was the son of Yixin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi was a son of Liu Yixin.

sentences.zh: 劉勉圍壽陽，垣閎攻合肥，俱未下。

translations.literal: Liu Mian besieged Shouyang and Yuan Hong attacked Hefei; neither had been taken.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian besieged Shouyang and Yuan Hong attacked Hefei; neither city had fallen.

sentences.zh: 勉患之，召諸將會議。

translations.literal: Mian was troubled by this and summoned the generals to council.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was vexed and called his generals to council.

sentences.zh: 馬隊主王廣之曰：「得將軍所乘馬，判能平合肥。」

translations.literal: Cavalry detachment commander Wang Guangzhi said: "If I had the horse Your Excellency rides, I could surely pacify Hefei."
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry detachment commander Wang Guangzhi said, "Give me the horse you ride, Commander, and I can take Hefei."

sentences.zh: 幢主皇甫肅怒曰：「廣之敢奪節下馬，可斬！」

translations.literal: Pennant commander Huangfu Su in anger said: "Guangzhi dares seize the commander's horse—he should be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Pennant commander Huangfu Su snapped, "Guangzhi would steal our commander's mount—he deserves death!"

sentences.zh: 勉笑曰：「觀其意，必能立功。」

translations.literal: Mian laughed and said: "Judging his intent, he will surely achieve merit."
translations.idiomatic: Mian laughed and said, "He means to win glory—I trust he will."

sentences.zh: 即推鞍下馬與之。

translations.literal: He then pushed off the saddle and dismounted, giving the horse to him.
translations.idiomatic: He dismounted and gave him the horse.

sentences.zh: 廣之往攻合肥，三日，克之；

translations.literal: Guangzhi went to attack Hefei; in three days he took it;
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhi attacked Hefei and took it in three days;

sentences.zh: 薛道標突圍奔淮西歸常珍奇，勉擢廣之為軍主。

translations.literal: Xue Daobiao broke the encirclement and fled west of the Huai to join Chang Zhenqi; Mian promoted Guangzhi to army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Daobiao broke out and fled west of the Huai to Chang Zhenqi; Mian promoted Guangzhi to army commander.

sentences.zh: 廣之謂肅曰：「節下若從卿言，何以平賊！

translations.literal: Guangzhi said to Su: "If the commander had followed your words, how could the bandits have been pacified!
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhi told Su, "Had the commander listened to you, how would we have beaten the rebels!

sentences.zh: 卿不賞才，乃至於此！」

translations.literal: You do not prize talent—so it has come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: You cannot recognize talent—that is why you are here!"

sentences.zh: 肅有學術，及勉卒，更依廣之，廣之薦於齊世祖為東海太守。

translations.literal: Su had learning; when Mian died he attached himself again to Guangzhi, and Guangzhi recommended him to Qi Shizu as Administrator of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Su was a scholar; after Mian died he followed Guangzhi, who recommended him to Qi Shizu as Donghai administrator.

sentences.zh: 沈靈寶自廬江引兵攻晉熙，晉熙太守閻湛之棄城走。

translations.literal: Shen Lingbao from Lujiang led troops to attack Jinxi; Jinxi Prefect Yan Zhanzhi abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Lingbao marched from Lujiang against Jinxi; Jinxi prefect Yan Zhanzhi abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 徐州刺史薛安都、益州刺蕭惠開、梁州刺史柳元怙、兗州刺史畢眾敬、豫章太守殷孚、汝南太守常珍奇，並遣使乞降。

translations.literal: Inspector of Xuzhou Xue Andu, Yi Inspector Xiao Huikai, Inspector of Liangzhou Liu Yuanku, Inspector of Yanzhou Bi Zhongjing, Prefect of Yuzhang Yin Fu, and Prefect of Runan Chang Zhenqi all sent envoys begging to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou inspector Xue Andu, Yi inspector Xiao Huikai, Liangzhou inspector Liu Yuanku, Yanzhou inspector Bi Zhongjing, Yuzhang prefect Yin Fu, and Runan prefect Chang Zhenqi all sent envoys suing for peace.

sentences.zh: 上以南方已平，欲示威淮北，乙亥，命鎮軍將軍張永、中領軍沈攸之將甲士五萬迎薛安都。

translations.literal: The emperor, the south having been pacified, wished to display might north of the Huai; on yihai he ordered Pacifying Army General Zhang Yong and Central Army Director Shen Youzhi to lead fifty thousand armored soldiers to welcome Xue Andu.
translations.idiomatic: With the south pacified, the emperor wished to awe the Huai north; on yihai he ordered Pacifying Army general Zhang Yong and Central Army Director Shen Youzhi to lead fifty thousand armored men to receive Xue Andu.

sentences.zh: 蔡興宗曰：「安都歸順，此誠非虛，正須單使尺書。

translations.literal: Cai Xingzong said: "Andu's submission is truly not empty; one need only a single envoy with a letter a foot long.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xingzong said, "Andu's surrender is genuine—a lone envoy with a brief letter would suffice.

sentences.zh: 今以重兵迎之，勢必疑懼；

translations.literal: Now to welcome him with a heavy army, he will surely be suspicious and afraid;
translations.idiomatic: Send a great army to meet him and he will surely grow suspicious and afraid;

sentences.zh: 或能招引北虜，為患方深。

translations.literal: he may be able to summon the northern barbarians—the harm will then be profound.
translations.idiomatic: he may summon the northern barbarians, and the harm will deepen.

sentences.zh: 若以叛臣罪重，不可不誅，則向之所宥亦已多矣。

translations.literal: If because rebel ministers' guilt is heavy they must be executed, then of those pardoned before there are already many.
translations.idiomatic: If rebel guilt were so grave that none could be spared, you have already pardoned many.

sentences.zh: 況安都外據大鎮，密邇邊陲，地險兵強，攻圍難克，考之國計，尤宜馴養；

translations.literal: Moreover Andu outwardly holds a great commandery, close to the border marches—terrain dangerous, troops strong, attack and siege hard to overcome; weighing it in state planning, he should especially be tamed and nurtured;
translations.idiomatic: Andu holds a great frontier post hard by the border—strong ground, strong troops, hard to storm. Statecraft demands that he be conciliated;

sentences.zh: 如其外叛，將為朝廷旰食之憂。」

translations.literal: if he rebels outwardly, it will become the court's worry of meals at dawn and dusk."
translations.idiomatic: if he turns outward in rebellion, the court will lose its appetite for meals."

sentences.zh: 上不從，謂征北司馬行南徐州事蕭道成曰：「吾今因此北討，卿意以為何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow this and said to Northern Expedition marshal acting for Southern Xuzhou Xiao Daocheng: "I now take this occasion for a northern campaign—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and asked Northern Expedition marshal and acting Southern Xuzhou administrator Xiao Daocheng, "I mean to campaign north on this occasion—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「安都狡猾有餘，今以兵逼之，恐非國之利。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Andu is crafty beyond measure; now to press him with troops—I fear it is not the state's advantage."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Andu is surpassingly cunning; press him with troops and I fear it will not profit the realm."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「諸軍猛銳，何往不克！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The armies are fierce and sharp—where would they not conquer!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Our armies are fierce—where would they fail!

sentences.zh: 卿勿多言！」

translations.literal: Do not speak overmuch!"
translations.idiomatic: Say no more!"

sentences.zh: 安都聞大兵北上，懼，遣使乞降於魏，常珍奇亦以懸瓠降魏，皆請兵自救。

translations.literal: When Andu heard that a great army was marching north, he was afraid and sent envoys begging to surrender to Wei; Chang Zhenqi also surrendered Xuanhu to Wei—both asked for troops to save themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that a great army was marching north, Andu grew afraid and sent envoys suing for peace with Wei; Zhenqi likewise surrendered Xuanhu and both pleaded for rescue troops.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，立皇子昱為太子。

translations.literal: On wuyin, the emperor established Prince Yu as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the emperor named Prince Yu heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 薛安都以其子為質於魏，魏遣鎮東大將軍代人尉元、鎮東將軍魏郡孔伯恭等帥騎一萬出東道，救彭城；

translations.literal: Xue Andu sent his son as hostage to Wei; Wei dispatched Pacifying-the-East Grand General Yu Yuan of the Dai substitute lineage, Pacifying-the-East General Kong Bogong of Wei commandery, and others leading ten thousand horsemen by the eastern route to relieve Pengcheng;
translations.idiomatic: Andu sent his son to Wei as a hostage; Wei sent Pacifying-the-East grand general Yu Yuan, a man of the Dai substitute line, Pacifying-the-East general Kong Bogong of Wei commandery, and others at the head of ten thousand cavalry along the eastern route to relieve Pengcheng;

sentences.zh: 鎮西大將軍西河公石、都督荊、豫、南雍州諸軍事張窮奇出西道，救懸瓠。

translations.literal: Pacifying-the-West Grand General Western River Prince Shi, Grand Commander of Jing, Yu, and Southern Yongzhou affairs Zhang Qiongqi went by the western route to relieve Xuanhu.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying-the-West grand general Western River prince Shi and grand commander of Jing, Yu, and Southern Yongzhou Zhang Qiongqi marched by the western route to relieve Xuanhu.

sentences.zh: 以安都為都督徐、雍等五州諸軍事、鎮南大將軍、徐州刺史、河東公；

translations.literal: Andu was made Grand Commander of Xu, Yong, and five other provinces, Pacifying-the-South Grand General, inspector of Xuzhou, and Duke of Hedong;
translations.idiomatic: Andu was appointed grand commander of Xu, Yong, and five other provinces, Pacifying-the-South grand general, Xuzhou inspector, and Duke of Hedong;

sentences.zh: 常珍奇為平南將軍、豫州刺史、河內公。

translations.literal: Chang Zhenqi was made Pacifying-the-South General, inspector of Yuzhou, and Duke of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqi was made Pacifying-the-South general, Yuzhou inspector, and Duke of Henei.

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史申纂詐降於魏，尉元受之，而陰為之備。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yanzhou Shen Zuan feigned surrender to Wei; Yu Yuan accepted it but secretly made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou inspector Shen Zuan pretended to surrender to Wei; Yuan accepted him while secretly preparing against him.

sentences.zh: 魏帥至無鹽，纂閉門拒守。

translations.literal: When the Wei commander reached Wuyan, Zuan shut the gates and refused to yield.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei army reached Wuyan, Zuan barred the gates and held out.

sentences.zh: 薛安都之召魏兵也，畢眾敬不與之同，遣使來請降；

translations.literal: When Xue Andu summoned Wei troops, Bi Zhongjing would not go along and sent envoys requesting surrender;
translations.idiomatic: When Andu called in Wei troops, Zhongjing refused to join him and sent envoys suing for peace;

sentences.zh: 上以眾敬為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: the emperor made Zhongjing inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor appointed Zhongjing inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 眾敬子元賓在建康，先坐它罪誅。

translations.literal: Zhongjing's son Yuan Bin was in Jiankang and had earlier been executed on another charge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing's son Yuan Bin was in Jiankang and had already been put to death on another charge.

sentences.zh: 眾敬聞之，怒，拔刀斫柱曰：「吾皓首唯一子，不能全，安用獨生！」

translations.literal: When Zhongjing heard this, he was furious, drew his sword, and hacked a pillar, saying, "I am white-haired with only one son, and could not keep him alive—what use is living alone!"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the news, Zhongjing flew into a rage, drew his sword, and struck a pillar: "My hair is white and I had but one son, yet could not save him—why should I go on living alone!"

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬子，魏師至瑕丘，眾敬請降於魏。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on renzi, Wei troops reached Xianqiu and Zhongjing asked to surrender to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renzi, Wei forces reached Xianqiu and Zhongjing sued for peace with Wei.

sentences.zh: 尉元遣部將先據其城，眾敬悔恨，數日不食。

translations.literal: Yu Yuan sent a subordinate general to seize the city first; Zhongjing regretted it and for several days ate nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan sent a deputy to occupy the city first; Zhongjing, stricken with remorse, fasted for days.

sentences.zh: 元長驅而進，十二月，己未，軍於秺。

translations.literal: Yuan drove hard in advance; in the twelfth month, on jiwei, he encamped at Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan pressed forward at speed; in the twelfth month, on jiwei, his army halted at Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 西河公石至上蔡，常珍奇帥文武出迎。

translations.literal: Western River Prince Shi reached Shangcai and Chang Zhenqi led civil and military officials out to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shi of Western River reached Shangcai, and Zhenqi led officials out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 石欲頓軍汝，北即入城，中書博士鄭羲曰：「今珍奇雖來，意未可量。
