translations.literal: Shi wished to halt the army north of the Ru but then enter the city; Palace Secretariat academician Zheng Xi said, "Though Zhenqi has come now, his intent cannot yet be gauged.
translations.idiomatic: Shi meant to camp north of the Ru before entering the city; Secretariat academician Zheng Xi said, "Zhenqi has come, but his intentions are still uncertain.

sentences.zh: 不如直入其城，奪其管籥，據有府庫，制其腹心，策之全者也。」

translations.literal: Better to enter his city at once, seize the keys and tallies, hold the treasuries, and control his vitals—that is the strategy of complete safety."
translations.idiomatic: Better march straight in, seize the keys and tallies, hold the treasuries, and control his vitals—that is the sure course."

sentences.zh: 石遂策馬入城，因置酒嬉戲。

translations.literal: Shi thereupon spurred his horse into the city and set out wine for merrymaking.
translations.idiomatic: Shi spurred in, then set out wine for feasting and sport.

sentences.zh: 羲曰：「觀珍奇之色甚不平，不可不為之力求。」

translations.literal: Xi said, "Watching Zhenqi's expression, he is very ill at ease—we must press our precautions."
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "Zhenqi's face shows deep unease—we must brace ourselves."

sentences.zh: 乃嚴兵設備。

translations.literal: He then arrayed troops and made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: He then tightened the guard and made ready.

sentences.zh: 其夕，珍奇使人燒府屋，欲為變，以石有備而止。

translations.literal: That evening Zhenqi sent men to burn the government buildings, intending a mutiny, but stopped because Shi was prepared.
translations.idiomatic: That night Zhenqi sent men to fire the government compound, plotting mutiny, but desisted when he found Shi on guard.

sentences.zh: 羲，豁之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Xi was a great-grandson of Huo.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was Huo's great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 淮西七郡民多不願屬魏，連營南奔。

translations.literal: The people of the seven Huai-west commanderies mostly did not wish to belong to Wei and fled south in linked camps.
translations.idiomatic: Across the seven Huai-west commanderies most people refused Wei rule and fled south in linked encampments.

sentences.zh: 魏遣建安王陸□宣慰新附民；

translations.literal: Wei sent Prince of Jian'an Lu □ to comfort the newly submitted populace;
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent Prince of Jian'an Lu □ to reassure the newly submitted people;

sentences.zh: 有陷軍為奴婢者，□悉免之，新民乃悅。

translations.literal: where troops had seized people as slaves and bondmaids, □ freed them all, and the new subjects were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: where soldiers had taken people as slaves, □ released them all, and the new subjects were heartened.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，詔坐依附尋陽削官爵禁錮者，皆從原蕩，隨才銓用。

translations.literal: On yichou, an edict ordered that all who had been stripped of rank and confined for adhering to Xunyang should be fully pardoned and employed according to talent.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou an edict pardoned everyone who had lost rank and been confined for siding with Xunyang, restoring them to service as their talents allowed.

sentences.zh: 劉勉圍壽陽，自首春至於末冬，內攻外御，戰無不捷，以寬厚得將士心。

translations.literal: Liu Mian besieged Shouyang; from the first month of the year until the last month of winter he attacked within and defended without, victorious in every battle, and won the officers' and soldiers' hearts through generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Mian besieged Shouyang; from early spring through late winter he attacked within and parried without, never losing a fight, and won the army's loyalty through generosity.

sentences.zh: 尋陽既平，上使中書為詔諭殷琰，蔡興宗曰：「天下既定，是琰思過之日。

translations.literal: After Xunyang was pacified, the emperor had the Secretariat draft an edict to instruct Yin Yan; Cai Xingzong said, "With the realm settled, this is the day for Yan to reflect on his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xunyang fell, the emperor had the Secretariat draft an edict to Yin Yan; Cai Xingzong said, "The realm is settled—this is Yan's day to repent.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜賜手詔數行以相慰引。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should bestow a personal edict of several lines to comfort and draw him.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should send a brief autograph edict to comfort and win him.

sentences.zh: 今直中書為詔，彼必疑謂非真，非所以速清方難也。」

translations.literal: If the Secretariat alone drafts the edict, he will surely suspect it is not genuine—not the way to speedily clear this regional trouble."
translations.idiomatic: A mere Secretariat draft will look false to him—not how to end this frontier crisis quickly."

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 琰得詔，謂劉輒詐為之，不敢降。

translations.literal: When Yan received the edict, he thought Liu Zhe had forged it and dared not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yan took the edict for a forgery by Liu Zhe and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 杜叔寶閉絕尋陽敗問，有傳者即殺之，守備益固。

translations.literal: Du Shubao cut off news of Xunyang's defeat; anyone who brought word was killed, and the defenses grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shubao sealed off news of Xunyang's fall; messengers were killed on arrival and the garrison tightened.

sentences.zh: 凡有降者，上輒送壽陽城下，使與城中人語，由是眾情離沮。

translations.literal: Whenever there was a defector, the emperor had him sent below the walls of Shouyang to speak with those inside; thus morale within crumbled.
translations.idiomatic: Each defector the emperor sent to Shouyang's walls to speak with the garrison; morale inside withered.

sentences.zh: 琰欲請降於魏，主簿譙郡夏侯詳說琰曰：「今日之舉，本效忠節。

translations.literal: Yan wished to ask to surrender to Wei; his registrar Xiahou Xiang of Qiao commandery urged Yan, saying, "Today's rising was originally to prove loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Yan meant to surrender to Wei; his registrar Xiahou Xiang of Qiao said, "You took up arms to prove loyalty.

sentences.zh: 若社稷有奉，便當歸身朝廷，何可北面左衽乎！

translations.literal: If the altars have a true lord, you should return yourself to the court—how could you turn north and wear the left lapel!
translations.idiomatic: If the throne is secure, return to the court—why face north and wear barbarian dress!

sentences.zh: 且今魏軍近在淮次，官軍未測吾之去就，若遣使歸款，必厚相慰納，豈止免罪而已。」

translations.literal: Moreover Wei troops are now close on the Huai; the government army has not yet gauged our intent—if we send envoys suing for grace, they will surely comfort and accept us generously; it is not only escaping punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Wei stands on the Huai; the court cannot yet read our intent—send envoys now and they will surely welcome us warmly; that is more than escaping punishment."

sentences.zh: 琰乃使詳出見劉勉」詳說勉曰：「今城中士民知困而猶固守者，畏將軍之誅，皆欲自歸於魏。

translations.literal: Yan then sent Xiang out to see Liu Mian" Xiang urged Mian, saying, "Those in the city who know their straits yet still hold fast fear the general's punishments and all wish to go over to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yan sent Xiang to Mian. Xiang told him, "The people inside hold on because they fear your wrath and would rather flee to Wei.

sentences.zh: 願將軍緩而赦之。

translations.literal: I beg the general to be lenient and grant amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Be slow to punish and grant amnesty.

sentences.zh: 則莫不相帥而至矣。」

translations.literal: Then none will fail to lead one another out."
translations.idiomatic: Then they will come out in chains."

sentences.zh: 勉許諾，使詳至城下，呼城中人，諭以勉意。

translations.literal: Mian agreed, sent Xiang to the foot of the wall, called to those within, and announced Mian's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Mian agreed, sent Xiang to the wall, called inside, and proclaimed his mercy.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，琰帥將佐面縛出降，勉悉加慰撫，不戮一人。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Yan led his officers out with hands bound in surrender; Mian comforted them all and killed not a man.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Yan led his officers out, bound in surrender; Mian comforted everyone and killed no one.

sentences.zh: 入城，約勒將士，士民貲財，秋毫無所失，壽陽人大悅。

translations.literal: Entering the city, he restrained the troops; the people's goods and wealth lost not a hair's breadth, and the people of Shouyang were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the city he restrained the troops; not a hair of civilian property was touched, and Shouyang rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 魏兵至師水，將救壽陽；

translations.literal: Wei troops reached Shishui, about to relieve Shouyang;
translations.idiomatic: Wei troops reached Shishui to relieve Shouyang;

sentences.zh: 聞琰已降，乃掠義陽數千人而去。

translations.literal: hearing Yan had already surrendered, they plundered several thousand people of Yiyang and departed.
translations.idiomatic: hearing Yan had surrendered, they seized several thousand people from Yiyang and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 久之，琰復仕至少府而卒。

translations.literal: After a long while Yan again served, reaching Junior Chamberlain before he died.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward Yan returned to office, rose to junior chamberlain, and died.

sentences.zh: 蕭惠開在益州，多任刑誅，蜀人猜怨。

translations.literal: Xiao Huikai in Yizhou employed punishments freely; the people of Shu were suspicious and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Huikai in Yizhou punished freely; Shu grew suspicious and bitter.

sentences.zh: 聞費欣壽敗沒，程法度不得前，於是晉原一郡反，諸郡皆應之，合兵圍成都。

translations.literal: When he heard Fei Xinshou had been defeated and lost, and Cheng Fadu could not advance, Jinyuan commandery rebelled, the other commanderies responded, and combined forces besieged Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Fei Xinshou had been destroyed and Cheng Fadu could not advance, Jinyuan rebelled, other commanderies followed, and allied armies besieged Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 城中東兵不過二千，惠開悉遣蜀人出，獨與東兵拒守。

translations.literal: Eastern troops in the city numbered fewer than two thousand; Huikai sent all Shu people out and defended alone with eastern troops.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern troops in the city numbered under two thousand; Huikai expelled the Shu natives and defended with eastern troops alone.

sentences.zh: 蜀人聞尋陽已平，爭欲屠城，眾至十餘萬人。

translations.literal: When the Shu people heard Xunyang was pacified, they vied to sack the city; the crowd reached more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Xunyang had fallen, Shu people clamored to slaughter the city; their hosts passed a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 惠開每遣兵出戰，未嘗不捷。

translations.literal: Whenever Huikai sent troops out to fight, he never failed to win.
translations.idiomatic: Every sortie Huikai sent out won.

sentences.zh: 上遣其弟惠基自陸道使成都，赦惠開罪。

translations.literal: The emperor sent his younger brother Huiji overland as envoy to Chengdu to pardon Huikai's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent his brother Huiji overland to Chengdu to pardon Huikai.

sentences.zh: 惠基至涪，蜀人遏留惠基，不聽進。

translations.literal: When Huiji reached Fu, the Shu people detained him and would not let him advance.
translations.idiomatic: At Fu the Shu blocked Huiji and would not let him pass.

sentences.zh: 惠基帥部曲擊之，斬其渠帥，然後得前。

translations.literal: Huiji led his household troops to attack, beheaded their chieftains, and only then got through.
translations.idiomatic: Huiji struck with his household troops, beheaded their chiefs, and forced a passage.

sentences.zh: 惠開奉旨歸降，城圍得解。

translations.literal: Huikai received the edict and submitted; the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai accepted the edict and surrendered; the siege lifted.

sentences.zh: 上遣惠開宗人寶首自水道慰勞益州。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Huikai's clansman Baoshou by water route to comfort Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent clansman Baoshou by water to comfort Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 寶首欲以平蜀為己功，更獎說蜀人，使攻惠開。

translations.literal: Baoshou wished to make pacifying Shu his own achievement and further urged the Shu people to attack Huikai.
translations.idiomatic: Baoshou sought glory for pacifying Shu and incited the Shu to attack Huikai again.

sentences.zh: 於是處處蜂起，凡諸離散者一時還合，與寶首進逼成都，眾號二十萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon uprisings flared everywhere; all who had scattered reunited at once, joined Baoshou in pressing Chengdu, and proclaimed a host of two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Uprisings flared everywhere; scattered bands reunited, joined Baoshou against Chengdu, and claimed two hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 惠開欲擊之，將佐皆曰：「今慰勞使至而拒之，何以自明？」

translations.literal: Huikai wished to strike them; his officers all said, "The comforting envoy has arrived and we reject him—how can we clear ourselves?"
translations.idiomatic: Huikai meant to attack; his staff said, "The imperial comforter has come—if we fight him, how do we prove our loyalty?"

sentences.zh: 惠開曰：「今表啟路絕，不戰則何以得通使京師？」

translations.literal: Huikai said, "Reports to the capital are cut off—without fighting, how can we get envoys through to the court?"
translations.idiomatic: Huikai said, "The road to court is cut—without battle, how do envoys reach the capital?"

sentences.zh: 乃遣宋寧太守蕭惠訓等將萬兵與戰，大破之，生擒寶首，囚於成都，遣使言狀。

translations.literal: He then sent Songning prefect Xiao Huixun and others with ten thousand troops to give battle, routed them utterly, captured Baoshou alive, imprisoned him in Chengdu, and sent an envoy reporting the facts.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Songning prefect Xiao Huixun with ten thousand men, routed them, captured Baoshou, held him in Chengdu, and reported to court.

sentences.zh: 上使執送寶首，召惠開還建康。

translations.literal: The emperor had him escorted and delivered, summoned Huikai back to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Baoshou sent under guard and recalled Huikai to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 既至，上問以舉兵狀。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the emperor questioned him about raising troops.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival the emperor asked why he had taken up arms.

sentences.zh: 惠開曰：「臣唯知逆順，不識天命；

translations.literal: Huikai said, "Your servant knows only loyalty and rebellion, not Heaven's mandate;
translations.idiomatic: Huikai said, "I know only loyalty and rebellion, not Heaven's mandate;

sentences.zh: 且非臣不亂，非臣不平。」

translations.literal: and it was not that your servant did not stir trouble, not that your servant did not pacify it."
translations.idiomatic: and it was not I who made the turmoil, not I who quelled it."

sentences.zh: 上釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor released him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，僑立兗州，治淮陰；

translations.literal: That year a refugee Yanzhou was established, administered from Huaiyin;
translations.idiomatic: That year a refugee Yanzhou was set up at Huaiyin;

sentences.zh: 徐州治鐘離；

translations.literal: Xuzhou was administered from Zhongli;
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou from Zhongli;

sentences.zh: 青、冀二州共一刺史，治郁洲，郁洲在海中，周數百里，累石為城，高八九尺，虛置郡縣，荒民無幾。

translations.literal: Qing and Ji shared one inspector, administered from Yuzhou; Yuzhou was in the sea, several hundred li in circuit, piled stones for walls eight or nine chi high, with empty prefectures and counties and scarcely any wild inhabitants.
translations.idiomatic: Qing and Ji shared one inspector at Yuzhou—an islet hundreds of li round, walled with piled stone eight or nine feet high, with hollow prefectures and counties and almost no people.

sentences.zh: 張永、沈攸之進兵逼彭城，軍於下□蓋，分遣羽林監王穆之將卒五千守輜重於武原。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi advanced troops to press Pengcheng, encamped at Xia □gai, and separately sent Feathered Forest supervisor Wang Muzhi with five thousand soldiers to guard baggage at Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi pressed Pengcheng, encamped at Xia □gai, and detached Feathered Forest supervisor Wang Muzhi with five thousand men to guard the baggage train at Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 魏尉元至彭城，薛安都出迎。

translations.literal: Wei's Yu Yuan reached Pengcheng and Xue Andu came out to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan of Wei reached Pengcheng and Andu came out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 元遣李璨與安都先入城，收其管籥；

translations.literal: Yuan sent Li Can and Andu to enter the city first and seize the keys and tallies;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan sent Li Can with Andu into the city first to seize the keys and tallies;

sentences.zh: 別遣孔伯恭以精甲二千安撫內外，然後入。

translations.literal: he separately sent Kong Bogong with two thousand picked armored men to pacify inside and outside, and then entered.
translations.idiomatic: then sent Kong Bogong with two thousand elite armored men to steady the city inside and out before he entered.

sentences.zh: 其夜，張永攻南門，不克而退。

translations.literal: That night Zhang Yong attacked the south gate, failed to take it, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: That night Yong stormed the south gate, failed, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 元不禮於薛安都，安都悔降，復謀叛魏；

translations.literal: Yuan was discourteous toward Xue Andu; Andu regretted his surrender and again plotted rebellion against Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan slighted Andu; Andu repented his surrender and plotted to rebel again;

sentences.zh: 元知之，不果發。

translations.literal: Yuan learned of it and the plot did not break out.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan learned of it and the plot never broke out.

sentences.zh: 安都重賂元等，委罪於女婿裴祖隆而殺之。

translations.literal: Andu heavily bribed Yuan and the others, shifted blame onto his son-in-law Pei Zulong, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Andu bribed Yuan heavily, blamed his son-in-law Pei Zulong, and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 元使李璨與安都守彭城，自將兵擊張永，絕其糧道，又破王穆之於武原。

translations.literal: Yuan had Li Can and Andu guard Pengcheng, himself led troops to strike Zhang Yong, cut off his grain route, and again defeated Wang Muzhi at Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan left Li Can with Andu to hold Pengcheng, marched against Yong, severed his supply line, and routed Muzhi at Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 穆之帥餘眾就永，元進攻之。

translations.literal: Muzhi led the remaining troops to join Yong, and Yuan pressed the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi joined Yong with the survivors and Yuan pressed the assault.
